sections.title: Introduction
Typical working process
Obtaining access to Arena
sections.text:
Arena platform is available at https://www.openforis-arena.org

Every user in the Arena platform has a specific role. These roles are described in detail in this chapter.

The platform limitations are as follows:

1 RStudio requires R (https://cran.r-project.org/). RStudio is available at https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/

Read more about requirements for R version and RStudio in this chapter.

●  The service is free and the maximum size of survey data is 10 GB.
●  Only the Survey Administrator can view the survey data size.
●  The maximum upload size of any file is limited to 1 GB.

In general, it is better to avoid uploading very-high resolution images into Arena, and to plan the amount of
incoming data.

There are two methods to get access to Arena:

Method 1. Become a Survey Manager2.

A Survey Manager can create a new survey and tailor it to meet your needs.
You can also use ready-made templates to tailor your survey.

To become a Survey Manager, go to https://www.openforis-arena.org/

and request access to the Arena platform.

You will next see the following page:

2 A Survey Manager is not a user role, but a user’s privilege. A role is always related to a survey. Any user can get
Survey Manager rights, but predefined access rights to a specific survey.

Fill in all information. If you are dealing with forest resource data or are a first-time user with no experience
with Open Foris Arena, it is recommended to start using a template: read more about them in this Annex.
Then send the request and wait for approval. It takes typically 1-3 working days until you get an invitation to
access the Arena platform. When you have the access rights to Arena, your role will be a Survey
Administrator for your first survey. If you do not find the emails from Arena in your inbox, check the
Spam/Junk folder, then add the sender (shown in the request access page) to your contacts or mark the email
as not spam, so that the next emails reach your inbox.

Method 2. To get access to an existing survey, ask for an invitation from the Survey Administrator. This person
can send you an invitation to new users by email. The Survey Administrator will specify your role in the
survey.

____________________________________________________

When you have access to Arena, type in your email and password. In case you have forgotten your password,
click Forgot password? to receive a password reset link by email (see Chapter 13). In the top-right corner of
the login page you can also choose the theme (Light, Dark or System default) and the language of the user
interface. At the bottom of the page there are links to the Arena website, to this user manual and to the
support forum.

If you are a new user, set first your user profile: click on your profile picture in the upper-right corner of the
screen and select My profile.

Here you can set up your title, name and profile picture. Read more about the user profile in section 3.3.

sections.title: Log in to Arena Mobile using QR code
sections.text:
Once you have logged in to Arena, you can easily log in to Arena Mobile by scanning a QR code generated
by Arena.

To access this feature, you must click on your profile icon in the top right corner and in the menu that
opens select “Login to Arena Mobile using QR code”:

A dialog like this will appear:

Open Arena Mobile and follow the instructions in the dialog; you will be easily logged into Arena, and you
will be able to download your surveys and submit data to the server.

sections.title: User profile
Two-factor authentication (2FA)
sections.text:
System administrators can protect their account with two-factor authentication: after typing the password,
Arena asks for a verification code generated by an authenticator app on a mobile device.

To add a 2FA device:

•  Open My profile and click Manage 2FA. The list of your 2FA devices opens.

•  Click New, type a Device name (e.g. My phone) and click Create.

•  Install an authenticator app on your mobile device (e.g. Google Authenticator or Authy).

•  Scan the QR code with the authenticator app (or click Show secret key and type the key in the app).

•  Type (or paste) two consecutive codes generated by the app in Authenticator code 1 and
Authenticator code 2 (wait 30 seconds before the second code) and click Validate.

After the validation, Arena shows 8 backup codes. Save them in a safe place: they are shown only once, and
each of them can be used only once to log in if you lose access to your authenticator device. Type copied
and confirm to close the dialog.

When 2FA is active, after typing your email and password in the login page, type (or paste) the 6-digit
Verification code shown by the authenticator app and click Verify. If you do not have your device with you,
click Use a backup code and type one of your backup codes.

From the details page of a device you can also Regenerate backup codes (the previous ones stop working)
or Delete the device.

sections.title: Main user interface
sections.text:
The view in the Arena main window depends on your user role (see Chapter 11). With the full Survey
Administrator’s access rights, the left side panel contains the following tools.

- Survey landing page

- Management of survey properties; delete a survey;
backup, export a survey; settings for map and security

- Design or edit data entry forms

- Visual view on survey hierarchy

- Visual dependency tree

- Management of categories (i.e., code lists)

- Management of taxonomic tables (i.e., species lists)

- Add, view, edit, clone, delete data

- Data queries, and access to data cleansing

- Map view & data editing; access to Earth Map and Whisp

- Export data into Comma Separated (CSV) or Excel files

- Import CSV/Excel/Collect/Collect Mobile/Arena backup data

- Data validation report, and access to data cleansing

- Create, edit, delete data processing chains,
run RStudio

- Show/stop RStudio Server (online process)

- User management, invitation of new users

- User grouping management

-Link to this manual

- Links to support materials and Arena repositories

- List of latest changes in Arena
- Terms of Service and Privacy Notice

- System Administration menus, shown only to system administrators at the bottom of the sidebar (see
chapter 14)

Preferred user interface language in Arena:
Automatically detected (from your browser
settings), English, Spanish, French, Japanese,
Mongolian, Portuguese, Russian or Serbian
(Latin). The same menu is available on the login
page.

Switch between the Light and Dark theme, or
follow your System default. The same menu is
available on the login page.

Lists work the same way in every page (surveys, records, categories, users...): click a row to open its item, to
view or edit it. In the records list, where the rows can be selected, a click selects the row and a double click
opens the record. With the keyboard, move to a row with Tab and press Enter to open it (Space selects it in
the records list). In each row, the view/edit button (pencil, or eye when the item can only be viewed) and the
delete button (trash) are the last buttons.

sections.title: Selecting and creating a survey (1/2)
sections.text:
In the upper right corner, there is access to the following functions:

Surveys page shows a table with all the surveys you can access. Select Only own surveys to show only the
surveys you own, or type in the filter box to search surveys by name, label or owner. The list contains the
following details.

Header  Explanation

NAME  Name of the survey. It must be at least 6 letters long.

LABEL  Label for the survey

OWNER  Name of survey administrator (owner)

DATE CREATED  Date when the survey was created

DATE LAST  Date when the survey was edited last time
MODIFIED

DATE PUBLISHED  Date when the survey was published

STATUS  Draft:  The survey is at the editing stage. It contains no data.
Published:  The survey is ready to store data. It can contain input data.
Published-Draft: The survey is ‘published’, but there are unpublished changes
in its structure (i.e., changes in attribute properties, new
calculation scripts or setting).

NODES  Number of nodes. This indicates the size of the survey.

CYCLES  Number of cycles in the survey.

LANGUAGES  Languages in the survey (ISO 639 language codes)

RECORDS  Number of records in the survey (across all cycles)

FILES  Number of uploaded files (e.g. photos)

CHAINS  Number of processing chains in the survey

Click Visible columns to show or hide columns. Click Export to Excel to download
the list of surveys.

New Survey allows a Survey Manager to create a survey in three ways:
1) Create a new survey from scratch, 2) Clone an existing survey or 3) Import a survey (Arena or Collect).

About naming of a survey:

•  The name should only contain lower case letters, underscores,

•  No space,

•  No special characters (#%&"?).

The entry box will automatically ignore the wrong letters.

Next, some more information on how to create a new survey.

Method 1: Create a new survey from scratch.
Fill in Name, Label, and choose the default language.

Next  steps  after  creating  a  new  survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and set in Description, needed Spatial Reference System(s)
(SRS)  and  survey  languages.
* Create the survey structure using the Survey Designer, test your survey and then finally
Publish it.

Method 2: Clone an existing survey.

Fill in a new survey Name and select a survey to be cloned. Cloning will only copy the survey structure,
not the data. A cloned survey will always be in the ‘draft’ mode.

Next  steps  after  cloning  the  survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties as needed.
* If the survey structure needs changes, use the Survey Designer, test your survey and then
Publish it.

Method  3:  Import  a  survey.
Import offers two options:

a) Import an Arena survey (.zip). An existing Arena survey, such as an Arena backup, can be
imported back into Arena (with a new name).

b) Import an Open Foris Collect survey.

Give first the name of the new survey in Arena. Check the Include Data box if the survey file contains
data and needs to be imported, otherwise leave it unchecked. The file is uploaded in parts: if your
internet connection is slow or unstable, select a smaller File upload chunk size.

Important: Do not use Export + Import (schema or backup) for cloning a survey! The reason is that
a published and exported survey will stay published when imported back into Arena. This means that
only a few changes are possible. Instead, if you clone a survey, the new survey will be in the draft
mode, and you can, for example, change/edit a taxonomic list.

Next  steps  after  importing  the  survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties if needed.
* If the survey structure needs changes, use the Survey Designer, test your survey and then
Publish it.

An Open Foris Collect survey can be imported from a .collect, .collect-backup or .collect-data file.
Note that after importing you should view the Collect Import Report at the Dashboard section. In

sections.title: Selecting and creating a survey (2/2)
sections.text:
addition, check out that all forms, tables, attributes and their properties are imported correctly.

Follow  these  steps  after  importing  a  Collect  survey:
* Go into Dashboard - Edit Info and edit survey properties as needed.
* Use the Survey Designer to modify the user-interface (as location and size of text boxes
etc.).
* Go into Dashboard - Collect Import Report, and fix the remaining (unresolved) issues.
* Test your survey in Arena and then finally Publish it.

Note: after an update of Arena, the surveys may be upgraded in the background. If you open a survey while
it is being upgraded, Arena shows the message “This survey is being upgraded, please retry shortly.”: wait a
few moments and open the survey again.

sections.title: Dashboard
sections.text:
The Dashboard section contains the following functions.

"Edit info" can also be accessed by clicking the survey name.

The Dashboard is a module of its own in the sidebar: open it from the sidebar or with Open dashboard on
the survey landing page. It is available to the users who can at least cleanse records (it is not available to
Data Editors).

Below the functions, the Dashboard shows a summary of the survey data. Select the period in Records
added in the last: (e.g. 1 Year); the cards and the chart refer to the selected period:

•  Records added in selected period: number of records added in the period; expand the card to see
the number of records by workflow step (Data Entry, Data Cleansing, Data Analysis, all time).

•  Contributors: number of users who added records in the period; expand the card to see the records
added by each user.

•  Storage: space used by the survey (shown only to users who can edit the survey); expand the card to
see the space used by the files and in the database, out of the available space.

•  Total records: trend of the number of records in the selected period.

•  Map: shown when the survey has geo (polygon) attributes; it shows the polygons of the records,
which can be filtered by owner.

•  Sampling Point Data Completion: shown to users who can edit the survey, when the records are
identified by sampling point data; it shows how many sampling points have been visited.

•  Activity log: recent activity on the survey (e.g. records created or updated); shown only when the
activity log is enabled on the server, to users who can edit the survey.

At the top of the Dashboard, the survey label is shown with its status (Draft, Published or Published/Draft)
and the survey name:

sections.title: Edit info
sections.text:
This section allows users to edit the metadata of the survey. The selections are divided into the following
pages: Basic info, Branding, Map, Document Layout, User extra properties and Security. System
administrators also see the Configuration tab, where they can set the total space available for the files of
the survey (Files total space (GB)).

sections.title: Survey basic info
sections.text:
Basic info contains information about the following survey properties:

Name:  Name of the survey in the database.
A Survey Administrator can rename the survey.

Label:  Label for a survey, a clear name for the survey.

View/Edit labels with other (selected) languages.

Description: Additional information about the survey (optional).

Field Manual Link: Full URL to the field manual of the survey (text) (optional). The URL
must be publicly accessible.

Language(s): Survey language(s). If more than one language is added, then labels need
to be given by all selected languages.

SRS: Spatial Reference Systems applied in the survey. Add here all SRSs which will be
needed  in  the  data  collection.
Hint: to add a new SRS, click the cursor into the input box and to see the options, type in
some letters of the EPSG code.

Cycles:  Inventory cycle(s) and timing(s). Note: survey times cannot overlap, so for
example this data is accepted:

Cycle for Arena Mobile: The cycle for uploading a survey into Arena Mobile in a
multicycle survey case.

The Map tab contains the areas of interest (see 6.1.6) and the sample-based image interpretation settings of
the Map section, read more about it in this chapter.

sections.title: Branding
sections.text:
The ‘Branding’ tab lets survey designers customize the visual identity of a survey: its primary color, up to
three logos, a background image for the survey landing page, and typography presets for the landing page
title and description. Branding settings are saved with the survey and are published together with the rest of
the survey definition, so data collectors and reviewers see the same branding once the survey is published.

Branding is entirely optional. A survey with no branding configured still displays a functional, unbranded
landing page.

The Branding tab is organized as a form on the top and a live preview of the survey landing page on the
bottom, so changes to colors, logos, background, and typography can be checked before saving.

Survey landing page

Branding is applied on the survey landing page, which is the default view when opening a survey from Home.
The landing page shows the survey title and description (from the survey labels), a button to go to Records,
and, when configured, the survey's branding: primary color, logos, background image, and typography
presets. A separate button opens the Dashboard, which has moved to its own top-level module in the sidebar.

Primary color

The primary color is the main accent color for the survey. It is applied to key interface elements such as
primary buttons and sidebar highlights, both on the survey landing page and while collecting data, so the tool
matches the branding of the project or organization running the survey.

Set the primary color using the color picker or by entering a hex value directly (for example, #2E7D32). If an
invalid color value is entered, the field shows a validation error and the branding form cannot be saved until
it is corrected.

Typography presets

Typography presets control the text size of the survey title and description as they appear on the landing
page. Choose the preset that best fits the length of the survey title and description and the overall look of
the branding.

Logos

Up to three logos can be uploaded (Logo 1, Logo 2, and Logo 3). All three are optional and independent of
each other.

Logo slot  Typical use  Displayed on

Logo 1  Main survey / project logo  Survey landing page and header

Logo 2  Partner or implementing organization logo  Survey landing page

Logo 3  Additional partner, donor, or country logo  Survey landing page

To upload a logo, select Upload image for the relevant logo slot and choose an image file. Once a logo has
been uploaded, the upload button for that slot is replaced by a preview of the image and a delete action; an
existing logo must be deleted before a new one can be uploaded in its place. Logos that have been uploaded
are shown, in order, on the survey landing page. Click an uploaded image to download it.

Landing page background image

A background image can be uploaded for the survey landing page. Background images are raster images (for
example, JPG or PNG) and are limited to 5 MB. Use Upload image to add a background image and the trash
icon to remove it; as with logos, an existing background image must be removed before a new one can be
uploaded.

sections.title: Document layout
sections.text:
The Document Layout tab is available in Dashboard → Edit info to users who can edit the survey. It contains
two groups of settings.

1) Document images

Images can be added to be shown in the header or footer of every printed document. Examples are an
organization logo, a project banner, or a footer with contact details.

To add an image, click the + button. In the dialog that opens, set the following fields:

Field  Explanation

Label  Label of the image (required, in at least one survey language).

Place  Header or Footer (required).

Apply if condition  Optional expression. It is evaluated against the root entity of the record being
printed. The image is used only if the condition is met.

File  PNG, JPG or SVG image, max. 5 MB. File names must be unique.

The document contains at most one header image and one footer image. For each place, Arena uses the first
image in the list whose "Apply if" condition is met, or which has no condition. This lets you define alternative
images for different cases. For example, you could use a different partner logo depending on the region of
the record:

●  Image 1: Header, Apply if: region == "north"
●  Image 2: Header, Apply if: region == "south"
●  Image 3: Header, no condition (used when neither of the above applies)

Click a row (or its edit icon) to edit an image. Images can be downloaded with the download icon and removed
with the trash icon.

2) Layout options

Option  Default  Explanation

Header on first page  Enabled  If enabled, the header image is printed only on the first page. If
only  disabled, it is repeated on every page.

Page numbering  Enabled  If enabled, page numbers are printed on each page.

Note: as with other survey settings, publish the survey to make changes available to all users.

sections.title: User extra properties
sections.text:
User extra properties section allows users to define properties that can be associated with the users working
with the survey. These properties can be numeric or text values.

Values can be assigned to the users in the Users list, pressing the  icon in each row; in the dialog that
opens, values can be specified for each user extra property:

User extra properties can be used in expressions like default values, validation rules etc., or to filter category
items or taxa in the taxon attribute search. The function used to retrieve a user extra property is userProp and
it can be used in default values, validation rules, items filter expressions etc.

sections.title: Security
sections.text:
Users who can edit the survey (Survey Administrators and Survey Editors) can view and edit the survey’s
Security settings, as follows:

Meaning of “can view not owned records”: If enabled, then a Data Editor/Analyst can view all other users’
records in the survey (on the list of records). If disabled, a Data Editor/Analyst cannot view other users’
records in the survey.

Changes to the Security options take effect once the survey is published, as reminded by the message at
the top of the tab.

The other options are the following:

•  Visible in Arena Mobile, Allow downloading records from server to Arena Mobile, Allow uploading
records from Arena Mobile to server and Allow uploading records with validation errors from
Arena Mobile to server define if the survey can be used in Arena Mobile and how records can be
exchanged between Arena Mobile and the server.

•  Allow merging records with same keys (e.g. records created in different Arena Mobile devices):
enabled by default. A record uploaded from Arena Mobile or imported with the same key values as
an existing record is merged into it. If disabled, such a record is not imported and an error is reported.

•  Notify survey administrators by email when records are uploaded from Arena Mobile: shown when
records upload from Arena Mobile is allowed, disabled by default. If enabled, every Survey
Administrator receives an email (in English) every time records are uploaded from Arena Mobile,
listing for each record the key values, whether it is new or updated, the user who created it, the
creation and last modification dates, the number of validation errors and warnings and its internal
identifier (UUID), together with the user who uploaded the records and the date of the upload.

•  Keep values of non-relevant attributes: when unchecked (default), during data entry the values of
attributes that are no longer relevant are cleared, after the user confirms it. When checked, those
values are kept in the record, even if the attributes are not relevant anymore.

•  Allow data entry users to preview the draft (not published) form: when checked, the users who can
enter data but cannot edit the survey (e.g. Data Editors) can preview the form with the latest changes
not published yet, for example for user acceptance testing (see 7.2.9).

sections.title: Map
sections.text:
The Map tab contains the sample-based image interpretation settings (read more in 9.7.2) and the areas of
interest of the survey.

Areas of interest

Areas of interest are polygons, for example the boundary of a forest reserve, of a stratum or of an
administrative unit. They are used in expressions to check if a location is inside an area, or to find the area
containing it. The expressions work also offline in Arena Mobile.

To add an area of interest, click Add. In the dialog that opens, enter the Name (used in the expressions) and
optionally the Labels, then select a GeoJSON file (.geojson or .json, max 10 MiB) with one or more polygons
in WGS84 coordinates. The polygons are shown on a map in the same dialog, so you can check them before
clicking Ok.

For each area, the list shows the name, label, file name and number of polygons and vertices. Click a row
(or its edit icon) to edit the area; use the other icons in each row to download its file, show it on the map or
delete it. Show all on map shows all the areas together:

Click Save to store the changes. As with other survey settings, publish the survey to make them available to
all users. The areas of interest can also be shown as layers in Data > Map.

The areas of interest are used with these expression functions:

•  geoDistanceToAOIBoundary(coordinate, 'area_name'): distance (in meters) between a coordinate
and the boundary of the area: negative inside the area, positive outside. For example, the validation
rule geoDistanceToAOIBoundary(plot_location, 'forest_reserve') <= 0 checks that the plot is inside

the forest reserve. Comparing the distance with the GPS accuracy, you can tell if a location is surely
inside, surely outside or too close to the boundary to be sure.

•  geoAOIContaining(coordinate): name of the first area of interest (in the order of the list) containing
the coordinate, or nothing if no area contains it. For example, use it in the default value of a text
attribute to fill in automatically the area where the plot is located.

Map layers shared with all the users of the survey (uploaded files or map services) are added in Data >
Map, with the Add data menu.

sections.title: Publish a survey
sections.text:
A draft survey needs to be published to make all recent changes available for the users. These changes can
be, for example, changes in attributes’ properties (as new validation rules), changes in form layout, new read-
only attributes or new calculation scripts.

Publishing a survey will make the following changes to the survey:

●  it will be available for data entry in the Data > Records section;

●  changes applied to the survey will be visible even in data entry;

●  deleted node definitions (e.g. attributes) will be permanently deleted from the records;

●  modified validation rules will be evaluated again and records re-validated (only for changed/edited
records);

●  for surveys imported from Collect: record editing will be available.

When publishing a survey, there is the following warning at the screen.

If Publishing a survey fails, you do as follows:

1) Open the Details section.
2) Scroll into the end of the error list.
3) Click on Export and you will get the error list into a CSV file (arena_NodeDefsValidationJob_errors.csv).

4) Fix all issues in your survey and try to publish your survey again.

Changes affecting existing data

If the survey is already published and you changed something that recalculates values already entered in
the records (for example the default value or the relevance condition of a published attribute, or an extra
property of a category or taxonomy used in expressions), Arena shows a further warning, Existing record
data will be updated, listing the affected attributes.

•  Click Publish and update data to publish the survey and recalculate the affected values in the existing
records. Values can be changed or cleared.

•  Check Skip data update (not recommended) to publish without updating the existing data: the
affected values are not recalculated until they are entered again, and the records may no longer
match the survey definition. In this case, type the survey name to confirm and click Skip data update
and publish.

sections.title: Export survey and data backup
sections.text:
The survey can be exported into a zip file with or without the data. In this way the user can create and
download a backup file. The zip file contains the following content depending on the selected option:

Export  Export + data (NO Activity Log)  Export + data (Backup)

Activity log contains the history of a survey. For example, it can contain data about who and when a certain
record attribute was updated with a new value, or who and when a record was upgraded from Cleansing
level to Analysis.

It is typically faster to export a survey without the activity log.

The Export + data (NO Activity Log) option is shown only when the activity log is enabled on the server.

A survey containing a calculation chain and result attributes can be exported also without the result attributes
(Export + data (NO Result Attributes), shown only if the survey contains processing chains). In this case, the
exported file contains the survey structure and the input data.

The options with data are available only to Survey administrators; Data analysts and Survey editors can
use only Export (survey without data), while the other roles cannot export the survey.

sections.title: Unpublish or delete a survey
sections.text:
In "Advanced functions", there are methods to unpublish a survey or delete it. Only users who can edit the
survey (Survey Administrators and Survey Editors) can unpublish or delete it. Unpublishing removes all data
from the survey but keeps its structure; to confirm it, you need to type in the survey name.

Deleting removes both data and the survey structure from the database. To delete a survey, you need to
confirm the deletion by typing in the survey name.

After deleting a survey, you have no active survey selected. This means that most commands will be
inactivated. If you go to the Home or Dashboard section, you will see the next text on the screen.

In order to continue working with Arena, you either need to select a survey or start creating a new one.

Clear activity log (shown only when the activity log is enabled on the server) deletes all the activity log data
of the survey, reducing the space it occupies in the database. The input data of the survey are not affected.
Also this operation must be confirmed by typing in the survey name.

sections.title: Collect Import report
sections.text:
If a survey was imported from an Open Foris Collect file, it gets a Collect Import Report. Otherwise, this
option is not visible for a survey. The Collect Import Report button is shown in the Dashboard, after Advanced
functions, to the users who can edit the survey.

The main difference between Arena and Collect is that Arena uses JavaScript (JS) language in expressions,
but OF Collect uses XPath language (for example within Required and Validation rules). So, when a Collect
survey is imported, all expressions need to be converted from XPath into JS, either programmatically or by
typing them in manually.

After importing a Collect survey into Arena, the Collect Import Report table shows all expressions which need
special attention, such as possible modifications. The import process can convert the most typical XPath
expressions into JS, but not complex expressions. Therefore, it is essential to fix all remaining issues before
trying to publish an imported survey.

The report table contains the following fields:

PATH:  path of entity/attribute in the survey structure.

TYPE: expression type (Default value, Validation rule, Relevance, Required if, Parent code).

EXPRESSION:  expression in Collect (Xpath).

APPLY IF:  XPath APPLY IF expression in OF Collect.

MESSAGES:  Validation rule’s user-tailored message in OF Collect.

View/Edit messages with other (selected) languages.

RESOLVED:  If blank, the import process did not do the conversion. Check all
unsolved issues before publishing your survey! Mark the issue "solved" (manually) after
doing the correction.

Tick shows that the issue is solved.

Edit the table, form or attribute properties.

The report table can be exported into an Excel file by clicking the Export to Excel button. This is probably the
best way to examine what needs to be fixed in the survey. In this table, the value ‘1’ in the column ‘Resolved’
indicates resolved cases, and those with blanks are not converted in the importing process.

Important:

A Collect survey can contain a validation rule which is logically incorrect but still working (!): a value is
checked against an attribute that is given later on the form/table. An example: in Collect, the XPath validation
expression is given for "Mechantable" (height) as follows:

In this case, the Collect Import Report shows this as an unresolved issue. The reason is that in this survey
"tree_height (Height [m])" is after "Mechantable", as seen below in the table. Arena cannot manage a
validation expression with an attribute being second in the hierarchy.

The second typical issue with a Collect survey is that Collect may not require setting in the key fields for
multiple-entry entities. In Arena, all multiple-entry entities must have a key (or keys).

sections.title: Working with cycles
sections.text:
Arena can host multi-cycle data. By default, all new surveys contain ‘Cycle 1’. Users who can edit the survey
can add, edit or delete cycles in Dashboard > Edit info (Basic info tab). Every survey needs to have at least
one cycle.

After adding, editing, or deleting a cycle, the survey should be published to make the changes effective.
Deleting a cycle will permanently remove all the records of the cycle!

When a new cycle is added, it inherits the survey structure (i.e. schema) from the previous cycle. However,
data structure between the cycles can contain differences, so each cycle can have individual properties such
as different attributes, form layout, etc.

If the survey contains more than one cycle, an attribute (with a specific name) can belong to one specific
cycle, or to preset cycle(s). Attribute’s properties (e.g., name, label, validation rules) are the same across
cycles, but an attribute’s position on the forms may vary.

More about cycles:

-  Each cycle contains its own records. A record cannot be common across cycles.
-  Settings for the Arena Map are common across cycles.
-  Categories and taxonomies are common across cycles.
-  Chains are common across cycles.
-  The Validation Report is executed only for the selected cycle data.
-  "Export + data (Backup)" will export data from all cycles.
-  "Data Export" into CSV/Excel files will export data from the selected cycle. In every table, the first
column indicates the cycle number.
-  "Data Import" will import data only into the selected cycle.
-  Within a published survey, records can be cloned from a cycle to a newer cycle (read more in Cloning
data).
-  Data processing with Studio can retrieve data from the Arena server only from the selected cycle,
not all data across cycles.

sections.title: Compare a survey with another survey
sections.text:
With Advanced functions > Compare / update from file you can compare the current survey with another
version of it and apply the selected differences. For example, you can design and test changes on a test

server and then bring them to the survey on the production server, without exporting and importing the
whole survey. The function is available to the users who can edit the survey.

To compare and update a survey:

•  Export the survey without data (Export > Export) from the other Arena server.

•  In the survey to update, select Advanced functions > Compare / update from file and drop the
exported .zip file in the box (max 20 MB). Instead of a file, you can also select another survey of this
server in Or compare with another survey on this server.

•  Review the differences and select the changes to apply.

•  Click Apply selected changes and confirm.

•  The changes are saved as draft: test the form and publish the survey to make them effective.

At the top of the page you find:

•  Select a new source, to discard the comparison and select another file or survey, and Refresh
comparison, to compare the same file again with the current version of this survey (e.g. after editing
it).

•  Fingerprint: codes of the survey definition (draft) of this survey and of the compared survey. Equal
fingerprints mean equal definitions. The first one includes the internal ids, so it is equal only for
copies of the same survey; the structural one uses names and codes, so it is equal also for surveys
with the same structure created separately.

•  A summary of the differences: elements only in the compared survey, changed and only in this
survey.

•  Show only differences and Hide layout-only differences, to filter the lists.

The differences are grouped in tabs (Survey info, Node definitions, Categories, Taxonomies, Files); only the
tabs with differences are shown. Select an element in the list to see, for each property, its value in the
compared survey and in this survey. A label shows the status of each element (Only in compared survey,
Changed, Only in this survey), and a warning icon marks changes that need attention, for example
removing cycles from a published node definition, which deletes its data in those cycles.

Each element has a checkbox to include it in the changes to apply. Note that:

•  Elements only in this survey are deleted if you apply their change, so they are never selected by
default. If you select deletions, you have to confirm them by typing the survey name.

•  Node definitions are matched by internal id or, when the ids are different, by name. When a node
definition could have been renamed, use Match as renamed to apply the change as a rename.

•  Some changes cannot be applied to a published survey, for example changing the type, the key or
the multiple property of a published node definition: they are skipped and the reason is shown.
Changes that depend on each other are applied together.

After applying the changes, a message reports how many changes were applied and how many were
skipped. Publish the survey to make them effective.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.text:
Entity: Data entities are the objects of the data model such as ‘plot’ or ‘tree’. These are shown in Arena as
forms or tables. Entities are containers for attributes and relationships between objects.

Attribute: A data attribute is a unit of information inside a data entity, i.e. it is a single-value descriptor for a
data object. These are like properties of data entities: for example, an entity ‘tree’ can contain the following
attributes: species, diameter, and age.

Node (object): A node is a basic unit of a data structure, and in Arena the data structure has the shape of a
tree. A node object is represented by a single node in a tree, and it can be an element node, attribute node,
text node, or any "node type"3.

sections.title: Attributes or entities advanced actions
sections.text:
Move the cursor upon the entity or attribute you want to edit, and an action button with the shape of an
“hamburger” will appear; pressing that button will open a menu with advanced functions as follows:

Note: node move or convert is allowed only if the survey has not been published yet, or if the node is new
and the changes have not been published yet. Exceptions: a published Integer attribute can be converted to
Decimal (see 7.2.4.5), and attributes can always be cloned.

sections.title: Attribute or entity move
sections.text:
An attribute or an entity can be moved into another entity.

By clicking on the item “Move [attribute name]” in the advanced actions menu will open a dialog where the
new “parent” entity for the selected node can be selected:

Select the entity where the node should be moved and confirm the selection by pressing the button “Move”.

Note: when moving an entity, only entities not descendants of the current one can be selected.

sections.title: Attribute clone
sections.text:
An attribute can be cloned into another entity. All its properties will be copied, including all the expressions
defined for Default value, Relevant if or Validations.

The operation is similar to moving a node; by clicking on the item “Clone [attribute name]” in the advanced
menu, a dialog to select the target parent entity will open; select it and confirm the target entity.

Note: since the cloning will copy the expressions defined in the source attribute, it may happen that some of
these expressions will be invalid in the new cloned attribute; in that case, after the cloning, the attribute edit
form will appear, thus allowing a fix of these errors.

Cloning is available to all survey designers, also for attributes that have already been published. Entities
cannot be cloned with this function; to copy an entity from another survey, use Clone Node From Another
Survey (see 7.2.4.4).

sections.title: Attribute data type conversion
sections.text:
An attribute can be converted from one data type to another. All properties that are compatible with the
new type will be preserved, including expressions defined in Default values, Relevant if, Validations etc.

By clicking on the item “Convert [attribute name]” in the advanced menu, a dialog will appear, allowing the
selection of the new data type as follows:

Select the new data type and confirm it by pressing the “Convert” button.

sections.title: Clone an attribute or entity from another survey
sections.text:
In the Form Designer, open the Advanced functions menu (top of the form) and choose Clone Node From
Another Survey. In the dialog, expand the source survey's form tree to locate and select the entity or attribute
to copy (either one can be picked, not entities only), then choose the Target entity in the current survey
under which it should be inserted, and confirm.

If the cloned node (or any of its descendants, when cloning an entity) is a code or taxon attribute, Arena
resolves its category or taxonomy automatically, without a separate step:

●  If a category/taxonomy with the same internal ID or name already exists in the current survey, the
cloned attribute is linked to that existing one instead of creating a duplicate.
●  Otherwise, the category/taxonomy is cloned from the source survey automatically, and a notification
lists what was cloned along with the node definition.

Note: the dialog lists the other surveys you can access and shows their published version.

sections.title: Convert a published integer attribute to decimal
sections.text:
Once an attribute has been published, its data type cannot be changed, with one exception: an Integer
attribute can be converted to Decimal, for example when the field teams need to enter decimal values that
were not foreseen.

Open the menu button (☰) of the published integer attribute: the menu contains Convert (besides Clone
and Delete; Move is not available for published nodes).

In the conversion dialog, Decimal is the only target type available. Select it and press Convert, then publish
the survey.

The values already collected are kept, including decimal values already entered (for example in Arena
Mobile).

sections.title: Units of attributes
sections.text:
Arena does not contain a property to set units for numerical attributes, nor automatic conversion between
the units. It is therefore recommended to add information about the unit into the attribute’s label, such as
"Diameter [cm]", "Area [ha]", etc.

sections.title: Automatically generating rows from category items
sections.text:
The rows can be automatically generated in a table, where the key attribute is categorical (code). The
“Enumerate” can be set to the entity (i.e., to the table):

The rows will be generated using the items defined in the category of the key attribute inside the entity one
row for each item). In the enumerated table or form, new rows or forms cannot be added or deleted, and
the key code attribute will not be editable. In addition, the key attribute should not have an “Items filter”
expression (because the items cannot be changed dynamically).

Note: a code attribute marked as “key” should be defined inside the entity, otherwise marking it with
“Enumerate” will not make any effect.

sections.title: Dynamic enumerated entity
sections.text:
Enumerate auto-generates one table row per item in the key attribute's category and disables manual
add/delete options. Until now that category always had to be used in full. Dynamic Enumerate adds an
optional Enumerating items expression to the entity: when set, only the category items whose code is
returned by the expression get a row; the rest are skipped. Leave it empty and Enumerate behaves exactly
as before.

The expression is typically built around the unique() function, which returns the distinct values found in a
multiple attribute or entity. This lets a table auto-generate one summary row per distinct value already
present elsewhere in the record, instead of one row per category item regardless of whether it's used.

Example: a table_source table where the field team logs individual measurements, each tagged with a
source_type code and a value:

●  table_sum is set to Enumerate, linked to a category “types” (items A, B, C), with Enumerating items
expression set to unique(table_source.source_type).
●  As the user enters table_source rows, table_sum automatically gains one row for each distinct
source_type actually used (not all of A, B, C, only the ones present).
●  Each table_sum row can carry its own computed attribute, e.g. value_sum with default value
sum(table_source[$context.sum_type == source_type].value), to total the matching entries.

Prerequisites

●  The entity already meets the standard Enumerate requirements: multiple-entry table, Enumerate
checked, with a categorical (code) key attribute linked to a category.
●  The category linked to the key attribute must already contain an item for every code the expression
can produce; enumeratingItemsExpression only selects among existing items, it does not create
new ones. Values with no matching item are silently skipped.
●  Like other node-def expressions, anything the expression references must be reachable from the
entity's parent context, and the entity cannot reference itself (self-reference is rejected by
validation).

Step-by-step

1. In the Form Designer, select the multiple-entry table and check Enumerate.
2. A new Enumerating items expression field appears directly beneath the Enumerate checkbox.
3. Enter the expression, typically unique(<path to a multiple attribute>) - e.g.
unique(table_source.source_type). Leave it empty to keep enumerating every category item, as
before.

4. Save the entity. While the expression field holds a value, the Enumerate checkbox is locked on;
clear the expression first if you need to switch Enumerate off again.
5. Test in Preview or a draft record: add/remove values in the source attribute the expression reads
from, and confirm rows in the enumerated table appear and disappear accordingly.
6. Publish the survey.

Behavior and limitations

●  Sync is incremental, by design: adding a new distinct value creates one new row; removing the last
row with a given value deletes only that row; rows for values that are still present are left
completely untouched, including any data already entered in them. Editing an unrelated attribute
does not touch the enumerated rows at all.
●  Rows still can't be added or deleted manually, only the generated set changes, and only in response
to the expression's source data.
●  If the entity itself becomes inapplicable (e.g. via relevant when expression), all its enumerated rows
are deleted, same as the existing Enumerate behavior.
●  Unchecking Multiple, or clearing Enumerate, also clears the enumerating items expression.
●  Same authoring and performance guidance as other Arena expressions applies: keep the expression
simple, since it's re-evaluated whenever its source data changes.

Every survey can be defined in multiple languages. Languages can be defined in the Survey Info section

When multiple languages are specified, every label field will have a small icon close to it: Pressing this

It’s always possible to add new languages and to remove existing ones, even when a survey is published
and data has been collected already; this type of change will not affect or break the collected data.

To translate the labels outside Arena, use the items Export labels (CSV) or Export labels (Excel) of the
Advanced functions menu: you get a file with one column per language. Fill in the missing translations and
load the file back with Import labels from Excel or CSV.

sections.title: Form preview (desktop and Arena Mobile)
sections.text:
The Preview button at the top right of the Form Designer lets you test the forms while you design them,
without creating real records. The main part of the button opens the desktop preview; the arrow next to it
opens a menu with the preview options:

•  Preview (desktop): opens a test record in the data entry form of Arena. The data entered in the
preview is not saved among the survey records. The form is shown in an orange frame with a Preview
Mode label at the top: select × in the label to close the preview.

•  Preview (mobile): opens the Mobile preview panel on the right side of the page, with an
approximation of Arena Mobile running in the browser with the draft survey. It is available to all
survey designers, when the server provides the Arena Mobile preview.

In the toolbar of the mobile preview you can choose Phone or Tablet, Portrait or Landscape orientation,
Reload the preview after changing the survey, and open the info button that lists the differences from
Arena Mobile on a real device:

•  dates and times are typed in a text field instead of the device date/time pickers;

•  maps are not available;

•  the location is taken from the browser (usually less precise than the device GPS);

•  photos and files are selected from the computer (no camera capture and no photo location);

•  the data is kept in memory only and lost when reloading; there is no records list, sync or export.

The preview can also be made available to users who cannot open the Form Designer (e.g. Data Editors),
for example for user acceptance testing of a new version of the form before publishing it: check Allow data
entry users to preview the draft (not published) form in the Security tab of the Survey Info and publish the
survey. These users will then see a Preview form button in the Records list (with the same desktop and
mobile options): it opens the form with the latest unpublished changes, and the data entered in it is not
saved. Survey editors (e.g. Survey Managers and Survey Administrators) always see the Preview form
button in the Records list, whether this option is checked or not.

sections.title: Multiple entities: automatic rows, summary and tables
sections.text:
Auto-create minimum items: for a multiple entity, this option (next to Multiple in the Basic tab) creates
automatically, when the entity becomes relevant or its parent entity is created, a number of entities equal
to the Min count set in the Validations tab.

Include in multiple entity summary (Basic tab of an attribute inside a multiple entity): the attribute value is
shown in the entity selector of Arena (the dropdown used to choose, for example, a plot) and in the entity
summary view of Arena Mobile. For attributes of the root entity the same option is called Include in
records list and adds the attribute to the list of records.

In data entry, the rows of a table (multiple entity displayed as a table) can be sorted by clicking a column
header: one click sorts ascending, the second descending, the third removes the sorting. Sorting by more
columns is possible. The sorting only changes the display, not the data.

Read-only values in tables are shown as text (labels), not as input fields; long values are cut with an ellipsis.

sections.title: Other attribute properties and layout elements
sections.text:
• Include seconds [time]: the time is entered as hh:mm:ss instead of hh:mm.

•  Display as [read-only text]: Text, Hyperlink (the value is shown as a link that can be opened) or
Markdown (the value is formatted).

•  Map marker color [coordinate]: color of the points of this attribute on the map.

•  Form Header: besides entities and attributes, the + button of a page lets you add a Form Header, a
title that divides the form in sections; choose its Header color (blue, green, orange, red, yellow) in its
properties.

sections.title: Expressions and expression editor (1/3)
sections.text:
Expressions are used to determine value. The resulting value is usually one of various primitive types, such
as numerical, string (text), Boolean, or complex data type.

Expressions can be defined using the “basic” expression editor and an “advanced” editor; the basic editor is
easier to use and allows to define most of the expressions you will need in Arena. The generated expression
will be a JavaScript expression.

The basic expression editor lets users define binary expressions, such as variable == some_value. For each
operand, users can specify whether it is a constant value, a survey attribute, or a function.

When Variable is selected, the user can select the variable/attribute from a dropdown list; when constant is
defined, depending on the attribute where the expression is defined, the value can be inserted in a text field
or selected using a dropdown list (e.g. if the attribute is a code attribute, the constant value can be selected
among the possible values in the related category).

When a Function is selected, the user can select one of the custom functions defined in Arena and specify
the parameters to pass to the selected function using a builder that depends on the selected function. The
possible functions are listed in the following table.

Function name  Description

categoryItemProp  Returns the value of the specified Extra Property of a category item having the specified
code

count  Returns the number of rows that matches a specified criterion

dateTimeDiff  Returns the difference (in minutes) from two date-time couples

first  Returns the first value or node of the specified multiple attribute or entity

geoCoordinateAtDista  Returns the coordinate at a specified distance and bearing from the specified coordinates
nce

geoDistance  Returns the distance (in meters) between the specified coordinates. The parameters can
Note: this replaced  be constant values in the format SRID=srs_code;POINT(x y) (e.g.
function “distance” in  SRID=EPSG:4326;POINT(12.89463 42.00048) ) or variables referencing coordinate
Arena 2.3  attributes, or also a call to categoryItemProp function to extract the location from a
category (e.g. sampling point data category)

geoPolygon  Returns a polygon in GEOJson format. It takes a list of coordinate values as parameters
(they can be constant values or coordinate attributes). E.g. geoPolygon(table.location)
where “table” is the name of a multiple entity and “location” is the name of a coordinate
attribute.

includes  Returns true if the specified multiple attribute includes the specified value

index  Returns the index (starting from 0) of the specified node among its siblings, e.g., returns
the current table row (or form) index number

isEmpty  Returns true if the argument has no value specified

Example-

Slop percentage%

Expression: 0

Apply If: isEmpty(plot_slope)

isNotEmpty  Returns true if the argument has some value specified.
Example-

Slop percentage%

Expression: Math.tan( plot_slope * Math.PI / 180) * 100

Apply If: !isEmpty(plot_slope)

last  Returns the last value or node of the specified multiple attribute or entity

ln  Returns the natural logarithm of X

log10  Returns the base 10 logarithm of X

max  Returns the maximum of the arguments

min  Returns the minimum of the arguments

now  Returns the current date or time

parent  Returns the parent entity of the specified node

pow  Returns the value of a base raised to a power

recordCycle  Returns the cycle of the current record, as a number

recordDateCreated  Returns the creation date and time of the current record as a datetime value. It can be
used in a text, date, or time attribute

recordDateLastModifi  Returns the last modified date and time of the current record as a datetime value. It can
ed  be used in a text, date, or time attribute

recordOwnerEmail  Returns the email of the user owning the record

recordOwnerName  Returns the name of the user owning the record

sections.title: Expressions and expression editor (2/3)
sections.text:
recordOwnerRole  Returns the role (in the current survey) of the user owning the record

“Row index”  In the Expression editor, this is a shortcut for "index($context)". Returns the current table
row (or form) index.

taxonProp  Returns the value of the specified Extra Property of a taxon having the specified code

taxonVernacularName  Returns the vernacular name (by set language code) of a taxon having the specified code

userEmail  Returns the email of the logged-in user

userIsRecordOwner  Returns a Boolean value “true” if the user editing the record is also its owner, “false”
otherwise

userName  Returns the name of the logged-in user

userProp  Returns the value of the specified Extra Property of the logged-in user

uuid  Generates a UUID (universally unique identifier) that can be used as an identifier (e.g., as
a key attribute of an entity)

Depending on the selected Function, a function builder may appear, letting you select the parameters quickly
(in the next image, the builder of the geoDistanceToAOIBoundary function, opened with the edit button next
to the function name):

Arena uses the JavaScript Math object that allows users to perform mathematical tasks on numbers. Math
is a built-in object that has properties and methods for mathematical constants and functions. See the full
list of Math methods here.

For example, constants:
Math.PI  = approximately 3.14159

Math.E  = approximately 2.718

and static methods:

Math.pow(x, y)  Returns base x to the exponent power y
Math.pow(2,3) = 8

Math.round(x)  Returns the value of the number x rounded to the nearest integer
Math.round(9.345) = 9

Strings are useful for holding data that can be represented in text form (see link to the String object). In
JavaScript, a string is a sequence of characters enclosed in single or double quotes, and single or double
quotes are the same thing. Some of the most-used operations on strings are to check their length, to build
and concatenate them using the + and += string operators, checking for the existence or location of substrings
with the indexOf() method, or extracting substrings with the substring() method.

For example:

"Sri" + " " + "Lanka"  = "Sri Lanka"

aString= "Vienna";
aString.substr(0, 4)  = "Vien"

aString.length  =6

aString.indexOf("nna") = 3, aString.indexOf("TX") = -1 (not found)

Similarly, Javascript objects Number, Boolean, Date, and Array can be used in the expressions.
Read more about expressions in Chapter "Examples of Expressions".

sections.title: More expression functions
sections.text:
Besides the functions listed in the table above, the following functions are available. In the basic editor, the
list of functions shows a short description of each function.

•  geoDistanceToAOIBoundary(location, 'area_name'): returns the distance (in meters) between a
coordinate and the boundary of the specified area of interest: negative inside the area, positive

outside.

•  geoAOIContaining(location): returns the name of the first area of interest (in the order defined in
Survey info > Map) that contains the coordinate, or nothing if no area contains it.

•  numberToWords(number): returns the number written in words, e.g. numberToWords(tree_no)
returns 'one hundred twenty-three' for 123. The words are in the language of the survey form
(English, French, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian or Spanish; English for the other languages).

multiple entity, e.g. unique(tree.species).

•  prevCycleValue(attribute) and prevCycleValues(multiple_attribute): return the value (or values) of
the same attribute in the record of the previous cycle. They work only in Arena Mobile, when the
survey has more cycles and the link to the previous cycle is enabled.

Areas of interest. The areas of interest are polygons (GeoJSON format, WGS84 coordinates) that you add in
Survey info > Map, each one with a name: use this name in the expressions. Both functions also work

sections.title: Working with categories (1/2)
sections.text:
Categories define predefined lists of coded values that are used across the survey to provide consistent
options for data entry, processing, and reporting. These fields are set up in accordance with pre-defined
classification schemes. However, the Survey Administrator is free to add, remove or modify them. Code lists
can be used to classify a wide range of attributes such as administrative levels, personnel, topographic
elements, accessibility, land use classes, ownership and many more.

There can be two types of code lists: flat or hierarchical tables. A flat table contains only one level with two
columns: code and label (or labels in all selected languages). A hierarchical code list can be used - for example
- for storing data by administrative units (e.g., province, district, village).

Categories (and taxonomies) are shared across all cycles within a multi-cycle survey.

Command buttons

Import multiple category tables (UTF-85 CSV or Excel files)
via a zip file.

Import a table from a CSV/Excel file.

Adding a new category

New code lists can be added in two ways: "manually" or by importing a table in CSV/Excel format.

To add a new code list, click on the  button. Then type the Category name. The arrow next
to the Add category button opens a menu to create a Sampling Point Data category or a category with geo
capabilities (see 7.5.3 and 7.5.6).

The category names should be unique. If the category name exists, there will be an error message, as follows.

Code items are always text (upper-case letters are allowed). To start entering codes manually, click Add next
to Items and fill in Code, Label and Description (optional). Items are shown as rows with index, code and
label: click a row to expand it and edit the item, move it up or down, or delete it; click it again to collapse it.

A quicker option to create a new code list is to import them using a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file. The CSV file should
be  in  Unicode  (UTF-8)  format.
This is the format for a flat table. If the survey contains just one language, then the file contains three
columns: code, label_[language], description_[language]

If the survey contains multiple languages, then the labels need to be given by the languages as follows.

with three levels: province, district, and llg (i.e., ’Local level government’).

In order to keep a separate record of the code list, it is suggested to Export the code list by clicking the Export

While the manual process for adding code lists is perfectly legitimate and can be used for simple lists, for
more complex lists (e.g. lists that have many items or with a hierarchical structure) it is strongly
recommended to prepare them in advance and upload them into Arena by clicking the Import button.

sections.title: Extra properties
sections.text:
Category tables can contain extra information (i.e. Extra properties), and they can work as lookup tables.
This ancillary data can be retrieved from other sources, for example from GIS.

Extra properties can be used for example in the "Items filter" expressions (Examples of expressions) and in
data analysis with R.

The next image shows hierarchical data in a CSV file. This can be used to import ancillary data for clusters
(level1) and plots (level2).

The extra properties can contain the following types of data: text, numeric or geometry point. In case of
geometry point (i.e., coordinates), the spatial reference system (SRS) must be preset into the survey (see the
Arena Dashboard section in this manual). A coordinate data split into three columns looks like this:

The best method of getting this type of ancillary data table into Arena is to create the table in MS Excel, Libre
Calc (or equal), save it as a CSV (in UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx) file and then import it. While importing, Arena asks
to select data type for each column because the default data type is ‘text’.

In the data analysis with R, all categorical tables are accessible (as a list of data frames).

sections.title: Sampling Point Data
sections.text:
Sampling Point Data (SPD) table is a special hierarchical code list with a fixed category name
"sampling_point_data". It can be used to define the list of sampling points, and their properties such as
coordinates of each sample’s location. Sampling point locations can be viewed on the Arena Map.

Here is an example of a Sampling Point Data for a forest inventory case:

SPD can be created easily by importing a CSV or Excel file that should follow the formatting indicated below:

●  levelX_code columns: 1 column for each level X (maximum 3 levels, e.g. if you have 2 levels, cluster
and plot, you will have a column "level1_code" with cluster id value and a column "level2_code" for
plot id value);
●  label_LANGUAGECODE columns: labels that will be associated to each item on the list; e.g. label_en
for English, label_fr for French; 6
●  description_LANGUAGECODE column: not needed, you can leave this blank!
●  location_x, location_y, location_srs columns: geometry point data as shown above;
●  optional: extra properties.

A spatial sampling point grid can be made in any GIS application, or by using a Plot Grid Generator, see Annex
6 for more information.

See the chapter Examples of expressions how to use and call Sampling Point Data with the help of expressions
in a survey.

To create the Sampling Point Data category, you can also use the arrow next to Add category and select
Sampling Point Data category: the category is created with the name sampling_point_data and the
location extra property, so you only need to import the file. In the category editor, the label This is the
Sampling Point Data category identifies it. If the Sampling Point Data category has no location extra
property (e.g. it was imported without the location columns), the category editor shows the warning The
'location' extra property is missing: without the location, the sampling points cannot be shown on the
map, exported to GeoPackage or analysed with Whisp.

Reporting Data tables

Reporting data tables can be used within analysis with R/RStudio (read more in Chapter 10). This is a flat or
a hierarchical table with the last column containing area information (in hectares or acres).

sections.title: Clone a category from another survey
sections.text:
In Categories, use ‘Clone Category From Another Survey’ (next to Add category, Export all and Import
categories in batch (from ZIP)). Pick a Source survey, then a Source category from that survey's category list,
and confirm.

Arena checks the source category against the categories already in the current survey before cloning:

●  If a category with the same internal ID already exists (i.e. this exact category was cloned into this
survey before, even if since renamed), cloning is blocked with a message identifying it by its current
name.
●  If a different category already has the same name, cloning is blocked with a name-clash message.
●  Otherwise, the category and its levels/items are copied into the current survey as a new,
independent category.

sections.title: Export all category tables
sections.text:
All categorical tables can be exported into a zip file with  button.

Choose Export to Excel or Export to CSV: the export runs in the background and, when it is completed, click
Download to get the ZIP file.

sections.title: Categories with geo capabilities and GeoPackage export
sections.text:
A category whose items have a location (a geometry point extra property called location) has geo
capabilities: the Sampling Point Data category is one of them. To create a category with geo capabilities,

click the arrow next to Add category and select Category with geo capabilities; to add the location to an
existing category, use Convert to GeoPackage category in the settings (gear) menu of the category editor.
The location extra property of these categories is locked; use Convert to simple category in the same menu
to unlock it.

The categories list shows the type of each category (Reporting Data, Sampling Point Data, GeoPackage) in
the Type column. In the category editor of a category with geo capabilities, the Export to GeoPackage
button exports the items, with their locations, into a GeoPackage file that you can open in a GIS application
(e.g. QGIS). The export runs in the background; when it is completed, click Download. Items without a valid
location are skipped.

sections.title: Whisp analysis of sampling point data
sections.text:
For the Sampling Point Data category (with locations), the Generate Whisp analysis button sends every
sampling point with a location to Open Foris Whisp for the analysis. Confirm the message: the analysis runs
in the background and it can take several minutes, depending on the number of sampling points. The
results are combined with the sampling point data and stored in a new category called
sampling_point_data_whisp (if this category already exists, its content is replaced).

sections.title: Working with taxonomies (1/2)
sections.text:
This section allows users to add one or more species lists by uploading a CSV (in UTF-8) or Excel (.xlsx) file.
The list should contain all the taxonomic species that the user will select from during data entry. Species lists
should be as comprehensive as possible and should be created using all resources available in the country:
local or global databases, taxonomical books, experts’ knowledge etc. For security reasons it will not be
possible to add species during data entry. Instead, additional species should be added to the CSV/Excel file
(by a Survey Administrator) and the updated species list uploaded to Arena.

Taxonomies (and categories) are shared across all cycles within a multi-cycle survey.

Adding a Species list:
A species list table should be prepared in advance following the formatting requirements indicated below.
The columns are as follows:

● code (required): alphanumeric (i.e. letters and numerals) unique identifier code associated to the
species,

● family (optional): family name of the species,

● genus (optional): genus of the species,

● scientific_name (required): latin name of the species (genus + [optionally] species name + [optionally
subspecies name e.g. Pinus spp. or Pinus radiata),

● lat (optional): synonym(s)7,

● vernacular_name (optional): such as local name or a timber trade name. The vernacular name
column must be named with the ISO 639-2 language code of the corresponding language (e.g. eng for
English, swa for Swahili, etc.). So, the column name in the imported file is just the language code.
Vernacular names can be accessed in expressions with the “taxonVernacularName” function.

● extra properties (optional): all columns not corresponding to the previous ones will be considered
as extra properties; e.g. ‘wood_density’, ‘species_commercial_group’, ‘protection_class’, etc. Extra
properties can be accessed in expressions with the “taxonProp” function or can be used in the "Items
filter" expressions (Examples of expressions) and in data analysis with R.

An example of a valid (tree) species list:

7 In an imported OF Collect survey, column "synonym" is shown as ‘lat’ in Arena.

Optionally, the Survey Administrator can specify other columns, such as the vernacular names of the species
using the language code (in 3 characters ISO-639-2 format, e.g. 'swa' for Swahili, 'eng' for English) as header
of these columns. Multiple values are allowed for vernacular names, and they need to be separated with a
slash ( / ) character.
Note: a species name (in the scientific_name column) can exist only once in the table. Similarly, each scientific
name should have a unique species code.

To add a new taxon list, specify first a name for the list in Arena. Then click Import, select the CSV/Excel file
and click Back when ready. The screen will now show the records present in the species list. Species lists can
also be renamed, deleted or exported. If needed, additional species lists can be created and uploaded in the
same manner.
There are two species names automatically added to your list by the system: Unknown (UNK) and Unlisted
(UNL). Avoid entering the same names and codes into the survey.

Taxonomic tables can contain extra properties associated with the species, e.g. dry wood density, timber
price, minimum cutting diameter, etc. (see the previous figure with an example containing "wood_density"
as an extra property). Extra property columns can be imported only via reading in a CSV or Excel file.

sections.title: Clone a taxonomy from another survey
sections.text:
In Taxonomies, use ‘Clone Taxonomy From Another Survey’ (next to Add). The flow and the internal ID/name

sections.title: Updating a taxonomy
sections.text:

When importing Excel (.xlsx) files (taxonomies and categories), cells containing formulas, rich text or
hyperlinks are read as plain values (the result of the formula, the text of the cell).
