sections.title: Getting a new template into Arena
sections.text:
Currently, only System Administrators can add new templates to Arena (see 8.3). If you are a Survey
Administrator and would like to propose a new template or suggest improvements to an existing one, please
contact the Arena development team at openforisinitiative@gmail.com. Include “Suggested survey to Arena
template” in the email subject line.

A template is typically based on a published and tested survey and should be sufficiently generic to support
a specific data collection purpose. As noted earlier, a well-designed template may include more attributes
than are required for a particular survey, since removing unnecessary attributes is usually easier and faster
than adding new ones in the Form Designer.

sections.title: Creating and managing templates
sections.text:
System Administrators can create templates and manage them from the user menu (click your profile
picture at the upper-right corner):

•  Templates: lists the templates (select Only own surveys to see only yours). Select a template to open
it: you can then edit it like any survey (Form Designer, categories, taxonomies, etc.).

•  New Template: creates a new template, from scratch (New Template From Scratch) or by cloning
an existing template or survey (Clone). Give it a name and click Create Template.

A template must be published before it can be used: only published templates are listed under Clone from
> Template when creating a new survey. Write a clear label and a description in Edit info: they are shown in
that list and help users choose the right template.

Processing chains can be cloned from templates too: when you clone a chain from another survey, the
published templates that contain chains are listed in the Templates group (see chapter 10.6).

sections.title: What are the data entry stages?
sections.text:
Arena implements a workflow which divides data processing into three steps (or stages): 1) data entry, 2)
data cleansing, and 3) data analysis.

1) Data entry stage

●  Enter data exactly as recorded on the field forms.

●  Data are neither interpreted nor corrected during this phase.

●  Invalid values (those marked as "error") must be checked against the field forms. If the
value was copied correctly, the value should be manually accepted. If it was copied
incorrectly, the value should be entered as it appears on the field forms.

●  Once all errors are either resolved or confirmed, the data entry clerk submits the record for
data cleansing. Before entering the cleansing phase, a copy is made and marked read-only.
No further changes may be made to this record by data entry staff (unless the record is
returned by data cleansing staff).

2) Data cleansing stage

●  Experts with knowledge of field conditions and data work with a copy of the data entered at
step  1  to  correct  or  remove  invalid  values.
Note: "Data entry" level users cannot edit the data which is at the cleansing stage.

●  If the data cleansing expert deems that the data entry task was not completed or that the
record contains too many errors, the record may be returned to phase 1 (entry) for additional
changes.

●  Once all data errors are resolved, the record may then be submitted for data analysis. This
locks the record so that no further changes may be made.

3) Data analysis stage

●  Records are locked. They can be viewed but not edited.

●  Records ready for analysis.

●  If during analysis data are deemed incomplete or incorrect, the record may be rejected and
sent back for further cleansing. Once updated and resubmitted, the record may once again
be available for calculation and analysis.

In the record editor, the current step is shown at the upper-right corner (e.g. Step 1 (Entry)). Click the
arrow on its right to submit the record to the next step, or the arrow on its left to send it back to the
previous step. Arena asks you to confirm.

In the Data/Records view, selected records can also be promoted or demoted with the Update records step
menu, as follows:

sections.title: Adding, editing and viewing records (1/2)
sections.text:
The Records section is used to enter, edit, view, and delete survey data. The main records view lists all root-
level records and displays key metadata such as key field values, creation and modification dates, step, and
the number of errors and warnings. Click a row to select it and double-click it to open the record.

The steps (=stages) are coded as follows:
1: Data entry stage, 2: Data cleansing stage, 3: Data analysis stage.

The command buttons on the right side are as follows:

Edit a record.  Delete a record.  View a locked record.

In the top left corner, the table has a checkbox to select all records in the view. If you have more than the
currently set number of records in the view (i.e., 15, 30, 50 or 100), this method will just select the records
of the current page (and not all your records).

Records can be displayed either unsorted  or sorted  , as follows:

Unsorted  Descending order  Ascending order

The user interface offers an input box for filtering the records, as follows:

The list of records can be exported into an Excel file by clicking on the  button.

The Export button opens a menu with these options:

•  Export list: the list of records, as shown in the table, as an Excel file.

•  Export data: the data of the records as CSV files (see Data export).

•  Export data summary: a summary of the data of each entity (for users who can analyse data).

•  Export selected records (Arena format): available when records are selected. The selected records,
with their files, are exported as a ZIP file in Arena format, that can be imported in Arena (see Import
data from Arena/Arena Mobile file) or in Arena Mobile.

Selected records are kept when you move to another page of the list, so you can select records on several
pages. The number of selected records is shown at the bottom left of the list. The selection is cleared when
you change the filter or the number of records per page.

Dates and times (e.g. Date created and Date last modified) are shown in the time zone of your browser.

Data entry is straightforward. You will see all tables/forms at the left side panel, and data entry form in the
main window at the right side. Start always entering data at the highest hierarchical level. For example, if you
want to save forest inventory data where the structure is "cluster-plot-tree", input the cluster level data first,
then the plot level etc. This helps ensure data consistency.

Arena does not lock the records (at data entry stages 1 and 2): users can work with the same data set, even
edit the same record simultaneously. All records are locked only when data are submitted to stage 3 (Data
Analysis). To avoid accidental changes, a record opened from the list is shown read-only: click Unlock at the
top of the form to edit it (and Lock to go back to the read-only view). A new record opens ready for editing.

Start adding a new record by clicking  button. The program will open a data entry form. While
entering the data, all data are automatically written into the database, i.e. there is no ADD-button!

All items that are set as "required" are marked with a red  symbol as long as the input field stays blank.
The red label text and the red symbol can also indicate that there can be an error in the data item. In this
case, Invalid record is shown at the top of the form: click it to open the validation report of the record.

In case of a multiple-entry table/form, such as tree data, the new record can be added by clicking the
button next to the table/form’s name. In tables, read-only values (e.g. calculated attributes) are shown as
labels, and long values are cut with an ellipsis (…).

There are two ways how to see the entities and attribute identifiers:

When working with forms that belong to lower-level entities, there is a text in the upper left corner showing

Species data entry can be handled so that you start typing in the first letters of the species name, or a code.
Then a dropdown menu will emerge, and you can pick up the correct name as shown in the next image.

There are two species names automatically added by the system when a taxonomy is imported from a file:
Unknown (UNK) and Unlisted (UNL). In order to enter one of these, type ‘un’ into the species name input

When attribute data type is ‘file’, the user interface looks as follows:

When a file has been uploaded, Arena shows the file name. When hovering over the name, a small snapshot

When a change makes some fields no longer relevant (their relevance condition is no longer met), Arena

sections.title: Deleting a record
sections.text:
If you need to delete a record, go to the Records section and view the list of records. You can select one or

more records and delete them by clicking the trash icon in their row or, after selecting them, the  button.

Look always at the step of your record: you can only delete a record that is on the Entry or Cleansing stage.

sections.text:
A row of a table can be deleted as follows: browse to the last column of a row. There you will see a trash

box  icon. Click that and message box will appear:

sections.title: Cloning data
Data Explorer and aggregating data (1/2)
sections.text:
Data Explorer is a tool for viewing data in the tabular format. You can view both input data and (computed)
result variables in the same table. You can view data in multiple ways (such as filtered and/or sorted), and it
can be exported into a CSV or Excel file. In Raw mode, users who can edit the data can also turn on Edit and
edit the data directly in this view.

Data Explorer can be used to aggregate data. This means that it can work as a reporting tool in "Aggregate
Mode".

Letter "M"  indicates that this is a multiple-entry attribute.

All data in view can be exported into a CSV or Excel file with the Export button.

The main controls of Data Explorer are:

•  Entity selector (left panel): select the entity (table) to view. The funnel button next to it filters the
attributes by data type; Search variable by name filters them by name or label.

•  Attributes list: click the attributes to add them as columns. They also appear as chips above the table,
where you can remove them or drag them to change the order of the columns.

•  Show/Hide Node Definitions Selector button: shows or hides the left panel.

•  Mode: Raw (one row per entity) or Aggregate (see below). In Raw mode, the Edit switch lets you
edit the data in the table.

•  Filter records, Sort and Export: filter, sort and export the data in view. You can also sort quickly by
clicking the arrow next to a column header.

•  View: display options (Show names, Show codes, Show total and percentage).

•  Manage queries: save the current query (entity, attributes, filter, sorting) and open the saved ones.

•  Table / Chart: show the data as a table or as a chart.

The current version allows users to view and export the computed result variables in the Data Explorer view.
Similarly, as imputed data attributes, computed result variables can be selected into the view, as below.

Data can be aggregated  to higher levels of the hierarchy. The aggregate mode contains two
sections:

1) Dimension. All categorical, boolean and key attributes of the selected entity and its parent entities.
The list also contains computed categorical variables, and these are tagged with (C).
2) Measure. All numeric attributes of the selected entity and its parent entities but excluding key
attributes. The list also contains computed quantitative (i.e. numeric) result variables, and these are
tagged with (C).

Multiple-entry attributes cannot be shown in the aggregate mode view.

For example, tree result variables, such as "number of trees per hectare" can be aggregated to a plot level,
or any upper level.

Follow the next steps to see the aggregates:

1) Select the entity (table) to report in the entity selector

2) Click Aggregate next to Mode.
3) Select the Dimensions to be reported. In this case Cluster ID and Plot no. are selected:

4) Select the Measures to be reported.

5) In the table, Sum is the default function. To change it, click the gear icon in the column header

at the icon  and change the
aggregate function.

Deselect Sum and select Average and Count.

And then close the Aggregate function window by clicking  button at the top-right corner (or Close
at  the  bottom).
In the result view, the DBH statistics look as follows:

6) More complex custom aggregate functions8 can be applied in the reporting, if needed. The
aggregation uses the Structured Query Language (SQL) expressions which is the fastest method to
run a database query on the Arena server. In the aggregate functions panel, click New under Custom
aggregate functions, enter a name and an SQL expression using the column names of the entity (e.g.
dbh), then click Save. The expression can contain only the column names of the entity, numbers, text
in single quotes, arithmetic and comparison operators, CASE WHEN … THEN … ELSE … END, FILTER
(WHERE …) and common functions (e.g. sum, avg, count, min, max, median, stddev, percentile_cont,
coalesce, round): any other SQL (e.g. SELECT, semicolons or comments) is not accepted and the error

sections.text:
is shown on the expression field.

After clicking Save, we can see the list of custom aggregate functions as follows:

The reported custom aggregates need to be selected (checkbox) in order to see them in the report
table.

7) Click Close.

And the results will look as follows:

8) Data can now be exported to a CSV or Excel file with the Export button  .

sections.title: Filtering records and searching attributes
sections.text:
Click Filter records to show only the rows matching an expression. Build the expression with the basic
editor (variable, operator, value, +AND, +OR), or click Advanced to write it. Expressions are written in
JavaScript syntax, using the attribute names: e.g. dbh >= 40 && total_height > 20. Use && for AND, || for
OR, == for equal and != for not equal.

To search text values, use text_attr.includes('abc'), text_attr.startsWith('abc') or text_attr.endsWith('abc').
Add .toLowerCase() before them to ignore the case, e.g. text_attr.toLowerCase().includes('abc'). Press
Ctrl+Space to see the variables and functions you can use.

Click Apply to filter the data. While a filter is active, the Filter records button is highlighted. The same filter
is used when you export the data.

To find an attribute quickly in a long list, type part of its name or label in Search variable by name, above
the attributes list.

sections.title: Totals and percentages
sections.text:
In aggregate mode, with a single measure, you can show the total of the measure and the percentage of
every row. Open the View menu and select Show total and percentage: a % column is added next to each
aggregate function and a Total row at the bottom of the table.

The View menu also contains:

•  Show names: show the attribute names instead of their labels.

•  Show codes: show the codes of the category items next to their labels (table view only).

sections.title: Exporting data as a table or as a data matrix
sections.text:
Click Export to export the data in view. Choose the file format (Excel or CSV) and the options, and click
Export. The options include Records modified after and Records modified before, to export only the
records modified in a period.

When the selected entity is a multiple entity (e.g. trees, or species of a vegetation plot) and you are in Raw
mode, you can also export the data as a Data matrix: one row for each species (or other attribute) and one
column for each record, as required by vegetation analysis tools such as Turboveg, Juice and Synbiosys. In
Export as, select Data matrix, then choose:

•  Rows: the attribute whose values become the rows (e.g. the species). Taxon attributes are exported
with their scientific name.

•  Second row attribute (optional): e.g. the layer, when the same species can appear more than once
in a record.

•  Key attributes used to name the record columns: each record becomes a column, named after the
values of the selected key attributes (at least one).

•  Values: the attribute shown in the cells (e.g. cover).

The Preview shows the structure of the exported table. If a filter is set in Data Explorer, only the matching
data is exported. Click Start export to generate the file.

sections.title: Charts
sections.text:
Click Chart to show the data as a chart (bar, pie, line, area or scatter chart). Charts also work with large data
sets: when there are too many items, the chart shows a random sample of them that always includes the
outliers, and a message tells how many items are shown out of the total.

sections.title: Viewing map data
sections.text:
If a survey contains a Sampling Point Data table or coordinate data, the locations of the points can be viewed
on a map in Data > Map. Point locations can also be recorded using the map view. Base map data can be only
viewed but not exported from Arena.

The map opens in a workspace with the following parts:

•  the top bar, with the Base map, Add data, Display and Tools menus, the Screenshot, Zoom to data
and Full screen buttons, and a search box;

•  the side panel, with the Layers, Records and Legend tabs (the arrow button collapses the panel);

•  the status bar, at the bottom of the map.

By clicking on a map marker, you open a pop-up window with the location of the point and the "Edit record"
button, which opens the record in a floatable form window on top of the map view. The Previous / Next
arrow buttons of the pop-up move to the previous / next record of the layer.

Markers in each layer have a different colour, assigned randomly: click the colour dot next to a layer in the
Layers tab to change it. Use Display > Marker labels to show or hide the markers’ labels; Display > Location
markers shows or hides the markers. The label contains the values of the key attributes separated by a
hyphen (e.g., cluster_id - plot_no, 1 - 1 in the map view above).

The markers (points) of the selected layers will be shown grouped in clusters. Each cluster of points is a circle
with the number of grouped points. Clicking on the cluster or zooming sufficiently the actual locations will be
visible as follows:

With the Base map menu, you can select the base map from several options (custom base maps added as
WMS / WMTS services or XYZ tiles are listed there too, see 9.7.5). In the Layers tab, select the layer(s) to be
shown: there is one layer for each coordinate attribute defined in the survey (Input data), one for each level
of the Sampling Point Data and one for each area of interest of the survey (see 9.7.8).

The maximum zoom levels are as follows9: ‘ESRI World Imagery’ 17, ‘ESRI Topographic’ 16, ‘ESRI Terrain’ 9,
‘UN ClearMap’ 8, and ‘UN ClearMap with labels’ 6.

Use the search box in the top bar to move the map to a location or to a record. Type coordinates in decimal
degrees (e.g., -6.1295, 37.587), in degrees, minutes and seconds (DMS) or in UTM (e.g., 37M 343814

9 see e.g. https://developers.arcgis.com/documentation/mapping-apis-and-services/reference/zoom-levels-and-
scale/

9322016) and press Enter; or type the beginning of a record key (e.g., 1) and select the record in the list.
The search finds the records of the layers shown on the map.

The Zoom to data button zooms the map to the data of the layers shown, and the Full screen button shows
the map workspace on the whole screen (press Esc or click the button again to exit).

The Records tab lists the records of the layers shown on the map, grouped by layer, with the number of
markers. Click a record to move the map to its location and open its pop-up; use Sort to sort the list by key.
The selected record is highlighted in the list. Drag the handle on the right edge of the panel to make it
wider or narrower.

The Legend tab explains the symbols on the map: record locations, groups of nearby records, the sampling
polygon and the UTM grid (when shown) and the added layers.

In the record editor, the map button next to a coordinate attribute opens the location in a smaller map,
with the Base map and Display menus, the measure distance tool and a coordinates search box. Click the
marker to see the coordinates and the elevation of the point; double click on the map or drag the marker to
change the location (if the record can be edited), then click Save.

The status bar at the bottom of the map shows the coordinates of the mouse pointer (click the notation, e.g.
Lat, Lon, to switch to DMS or UTM), the current zoom level, the scale and the number of records in view:

The sample-based image interpretation allows users to visually collect data from map and satellite images

sections.title: Google Earth Engine queries via Earth Map
sections.text:
Earth Map (EM) is a free Open Foris tool developed by FAO in the framework of the FAO – Google partnership.
It allows users to easily visualize, process and analyze multi-temporal satellite imagery and global datasets on
climate, vegetation, fires, biodiversity, geo-social and other topics, using the Google Earth Engine (GEE) data
without coding. Users need no prior knowledge of remote sensing or Geographical Information Systems (GIS).

Currently, we can make a GEE query for a polygon in EM. The polygon submitted from Arena is the same as
defined in the survey settings, see Sample-based image interpretation. This polygon is called Area of Interest
(AOI) in Earth Map11.

11 Earth Map uses GeoJSON geometries and there is no circle geometry. Therefore Arena "simulates" a circle with a
multi-vertex polygon in Earth Map.

If sample-based image interpretation is not enabled in Survey info (Map tab), then Arena submits a polygon
of 100m x 100m to Earth Map.

The following picture shows a circular sampling polygon in Arena’s Map view.

When clicking on a point marker on the map, you will get a pop-up with the  button. By clicking
on this button, Arena opens a new web page with connection to Earth Map. First, you need to sign in and
there are the following options:

With the last option, you can sign in without giving any information.

The same polygon submitted to EM looks as follows (with a query).

You can run GEE queries for your AOI by using the Statistics tools on the right side of the page.

You can get multitemporal results as shown in the following picture.

sections.title: Polygon data on the map view
sections.text:
Users can upload polygon (or point and line) layers to the map view: open the Add data menu and choose
Upload KML, KMZ or Shapefile…, then select the file.

Arena’s map can show KML, KMZ, GeoJSON (.geojson or .json) or zipped Shapefile (.zip) files, up to 50 MB
each, on top of the base map (or satellite image), as shown in the next images. After the upload, the map
zooms to the content of the file. KML points without an icon style are shown with the default marker.

Uploaded files are listed in the Uploaded files group of the Layers tab: use the checkbox to show or hide a
file, the slider below it to change its opacity and the × button to remove it. You can also upload several files
into the Arena map view, if needed.

Note: the uploaded files are not stored anywhere. So, if you refresh the web browser window, all uploaded
layers disappear. To share a map layer with the other users of the survey, add it as a WMS / WMTS service
or XYZ tiles (see 9.7.5).

sections.title: WMS / WMTS services and XYZ tiles
sections.text:
You can add layers published by map servers, for example national forest cover maps or recent satellite
mosaics. Open the Add data menu and choose Add a WMS / WMTS service…:

•  Service URL: the GetCapabilities URL of a WMS or WMTS service, or an XYZ tile template containing
{z}/{x}/{y} (e.g., https://tiles.example.org/forest-cover/{z}/{x}/{y}.png). Click Load layers: for a WMS
/ WMTS service, select the layers to add in the list (only layers available in Web Mercator can be
added); an XYZ template needs no capabilities;

•  Add as: Overlay layer (shown over the base map, listed in the Layers tab, group Custom (WMS /
WMTS)) or Base map (replaces the base map, listed in the Base map menu);

•  Display name, Image format (PNG transparent or JPEG, when the service offers both), Opacity and
Attribution;

•  Who sees it: Everyone in this survey (the layer is saved in the survey and shown on the map of all its
users; available to users who can edit the survey) or Only me (saved for you only).

Click Add 1 overlay (or Add 1 base map). Unlike uploaded files, these layers are kept when you reopen the
map. To remove an overlay, click the × button next to it in the Layers tab; to remove a custom base map,
select it and use Remove selected custom base map in the Base map menu. Only users who can edit the
survey can remove the layers shared with everyone: for other users the layer is hidden until the map is
reopened.

Note: services that use http (not https) may be blocked by the browser.

sections.title: Measuring distances and areas
sections.text:
Open the Tools menu and choose Measure distance or Measure area:

Click on the map to add points and double-click to finish. The measure bar at the top of the map shows the
total distance (or the area and the perimeter); you can switch between Distance and Area and choose the
Units (Automatic, meters, kilometers, square meters, hectares or square kilometers). Click Done (or press
Esc) to end the measurement.

sections.title: Map screenshots
sections.text:
Click the Screenshot button (camera icon) in the top bar to save an image of the map. The Map screenshot
dialog shows a preview and the following options:

•  Capture: Current view or Fit to plot (the map centred on the selected plot);

•  Include: Markers and measurements, Scale bar and north arrow, and a stamp with Plot, date,
coordinates, base map;

•  Save to: Attach to a plot record (the image is saved in an image attribute of the plot: choose the Plot
record, the Image attribute and the File name) or Download only (PNG file on this computer).

Click Save (or Also download to save it in the record and download it too). Images saved in a record are
available to the field teams in Arena Mobile once they download the record. The Plot record list shows only
the plots visible on the map when the dialog is opened, nearest to the centre first. Only the image
attributes of the plot that you can edit and that have the Allow saving screen capture in map view
property checked in the form designer are listed. Base map tiles whose server does not allow it are left out
of the screenshot.

sections.title: Areas of interest on the map
sections.text:
The areas of interest defined in Survey info, Map tab (GeoJSON polygons used, for example, by the
expression functions geoDistanceToAOIBoundary and geoAOIContaining) are available as layers in Data >
Map, in the Areas of interest group of the Layers tab. Check an area to show it on the map, e.g., to see
which plots fall inside it.

sections.title: Data export
sections.text:
Data of the current survey can be exported into a zip file that contains several CSV or Excel files. In the case
of multicycle data, the selected cycle’s data will be exported or there is an option to export all data.
The zip file contains all attributes grouped by entities. In the left side menu, select Data > Data Export. There
are the following options for exporting data.

Options marked with an asterisk (*) are not compatible with data import: files exported with them cannot
be imported back into Arena. Include result variables is shown only to users who can use the analysis,
Include data from all cycles only in multi-cycle surveys and Include internal UUIDs only to system
administrators.

You can also export data from Data Explorer (see 9.6.3) and the selected or filtered records from the
records list.

Options:

File format: Excel (.xlsx) / CSV (.csv)

categorical data, export both code and

2) Include ancestor attributes: include the

The next image shows an exported file containing forest inventory data.

The first column in each table is showing the cycle (‘record_cycle’).

sections.title: Data import
Importing data from CSV or Excel file (1/2)
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be provided as a .CSV (in Unicode, UTF-8; column separator is comma) or Excel
file (.xlsx). Each file to be imported can contain data of one entity (or multiple attribute). In Excel files, cells
with formulas, rich text or hyperlinks are read as plain values (the result of the formula, the text of the cell).
The data import contains several steps.

STEP 1. Select the cycle

In case of a multicycle survey, the user has to select the target cycle (read more about cycles here).

STEP 2. Select Import Type gives two options as follows:

-  Update existing records: select this method if the records are already entered and you can see them
in the records list (Data → Records), but you need to add missing data under the root entity, or you
need to update existing data.
-  Insert new records: select this method if the survey is blank (i.e., no records yet), or the records to
be imported are all new ones. Only the root level data can be imported as new records. All imported
new records go into the Entry stage level.

For example, in the following survey "CLUSTER" is the root level entity, and a file to be imported should
contain "cluster data" only.

STEP 3. Select entity

Select the target entity (or multiple attribute) to be updated from the hierarchy view under Import into
multiple entity or attribute, by clicking on its name. With Insert new records, the root entity is selected
automatically.

Click the link below the hierarchy view (Show names, Show labels and names, Show labels) to switch between
labels, names, or labels and names:

(Default view)

With Update existing records, click Options to show the following options:

1) Allow/Prevent adding new entities, such as new
sample plots into the database. [default: Allow]
2) Allow/Prevent updating records that are locked
(i.e. in the Analysis stage). [default: Prevent] 3)
Include files: import a .zip archive with the data file
and the associated files (see Step 4b). 4) Delete
selected entity's data in all records: all the
instances of the selected entity, and their
descendants, are deleted in all records before the
new ones are inserted. Options 3 and 4 are
available to system administrators only; option 4 is
not available for the root entity.

STEP 4a. Select file

Click on this box to select a file to be imported, or drag and drop a file here:

It is recommended to use the data import (CSV/Excel) templates. Select the entity in the hierarchy view, then
click Download template and choose CSV or Excel. Download all templates gets the templates of all the
entities in a single file. Do not add other columns: for example, the label columns (e.g. land_use_label) of a
data export are reported as invalid columns.

See in the next table information about data types to be imported:

Data type  Format

quotes. E.g. "The plot falls into a lake, not accessed"

Categorical, Taxon  code (these are read in as texts). For key taxon attributes
only the code column is required; the scientific and

or just an EPSG number

-attribute_name_x: numeric

-attribute_name_y: numeric

- attribute_name_file_name: the file name of the associated
file (e.g. photo.jpg), exactly matching a file provided in the
“files” subfolder inside the archive uploaded in Step 5
below. Leave the cell blank if no file applies to that record.

Multiple entry attributes  Import these as separate CSV/Excel tables, after importing
the parent entity table

sections.title: Importing data from CSV or Excel file (2/2)
sections.text:
After selecting a file, the file can be validated in order to detect possible incompatibles with the target entity
in the survey. The validation process only checks that the file contains valid data according to the data type of
each attribute. Hence, this validation will not for example check that a numeric value is matching the (input)
validation rule set for an attribute.

STEP 4b. Upload the associated files

If the entity being imported contains one or more file-type attributes (for example, a photo attached to a plot
or tree record), the actual files are not embedded in the CSV/Excel file; the data file only carries the file name
in the corresponding column, as shown in the Data Type table above.

To bring the files themselves into Arena together with the tabular data:

1. Prepare a folder where you will put both the data file in tabular format (CSV/Excel file) and all the
files referenced in the file-attribute column(s) of your data file;
2. Copy the data file (.csv or .xlsx) inside the just prepared folder;
3. Copy all the files referenced in the file-attribute column(s) of your CSV/Excel file into a subfolder
called “files”; file names inside the archive must match exactly the file names listed in the CSV/Excel
file (case-sensitive);
4. Compress all the content of the folder (not the folder itself, but its content, that is the data file and
the “files” subfolder) into a single .zip archive.
5. In the import wizard, choose Update existing records, open Options and select Include files (system
administrators only), then use the file upload box to select or drag and drop this .zip archive.

Arena stores each uploaded file against the correct record and file attribute automatically.

Previously imported files are replaced accordingly.

Tip

Keep the total size of the .zip archive and of each individual file within Arena's general upload limits.

For large photo sets, consider splitting the import into smaller batches by entity or by cycle.

Step 4c. Validate

After selecting the file, click Validate to detect possible incompatibilities with the target entity in the survey.
The validation process checks that the file contains valid data according to the data type of each attribute,
including, for file attributes, that every referenced file name is present in the uploaded archive.

It does not check, for example, that a numeric value satisfies the input validation rule set for that attribute.

When the validation finds errors, they are listed with the row number of the file and the error message.
Click Export to download the list of errors.

STEP 5. Start import

Click on the  button.

Confirm with Ok: the import cannot be rolled back. A progress bar shows the rows being processed, with
the elapsed and remaining time; click Details to see the progress of each step.

When the import is complete, a summary shows the number of rows processed, records created and
updated, entities created and deleted and values updated. If the import completes with errors, the errors
are listed in the same way as in the validation, and they can be exported.

sections.title: Import data from Collect/Collect Mobile file
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be in .collect-data or .collect-backup format.

If a survey is created in OF Collect, and this survey is imported into Arena and published, data can also be
imported into the Arena (later). This enables collection of data using OF Collect Mobile in data collection.

The checkbox "delete all records before import" means that all records (of the selected cycle) in the target
survey will be deleted. Be cautious while using this selection!

Selection "Force import from another survey" allows users to import data from a collect-data file, which may
have different survey name in Collect than in Arena, but the same schema (i.e. source and target schemas
match).

sections.title: Import data from Arena/Arena Mobile file
sections.text:
Data to be imported must be in .zip format and earlier exported from Arena or Arena Mobile (in Arena: Data
→ Records, select the records, then Export → Export selected records (Arena format)). The survey structures
must match between the target survey and in the file to be imported.

The conflict resolution strategy means that the user needs to decide what to do in a case where the same
record, or a record with the same key attributes, is already in the database.

It contains three options:

1. Skip if already existing: the record is skipped if it already exists in the database;
2. Overwrite if updated: the existing record is overwritten with the imported data, if the imported
record was modified more recently;
3. Merge records: the data from the imported file will be attached to the existing record (see Merging
data). By this means, for example a missing tree (entity) data can be imported into the records.

A record in the file matches an existing record when it has the same UUID or the same key attribute values,
also when the keys are codes of large categories or taxonomies: in that case the records are merged (or
skipped, or overwritten) instead of being duplicated. Merging records with the same keys but different
UUIDs (e.g. records created with different Arena Mobile devices) can be disabled in the survey security
settings (see Merging data).

The other options are:

•  Ignore missing files: import the records even if some of the files they reference are not in the .zip
file. Files already stored on the server do not need to be in the file again: Arena Mobile, for example,
does not upload the files that the server already has.

•  File upload chunk size: size of the parts in which the file is uploaded; use a smaller size with slow or
unstable connections.

Select the file and click Generate preview. The Import preview shows, for each record in the file, its key
attributes, the cycle, whether it already exists, the action that will be applied (Insert, Overwrite, Merge or
Skip) and the modification dates of the existing and the imported record. Unselect the records you do not
want to import, then click Import selected records and confirm. Records marked as Skip cannot be
selected.

If you cancel the import while it is running, it stops after the record being processed. At the end, a summary
shows the number of records processed, created, updated and skipped. Files with large records are
imported quickly.

sections.title: Validation report
sections.text:
Errors in data can be detected by several means. While editing the data in Data Records, there can be an

error message  indicating that there is something wrong in the data. However, there is no
easy way to find the erroneous data in the Data Records. So, for searching and browsing the erroneous data,
we should use the Validation Report tool.

The data validation report is a table that is created by running through all data validation checks in the survey.
It is essential to run this report and fix all errors in the data before the data enters the Analysis phase. Note:

if your data are already at the Analysis step  , you cannot edit the records. You need to
submit the record back to Step 2.

In case of a multi-cycle dataset, the validation is executed for the selected cycle’s data only.

The validation report can look as follows:

The validation report shows all records that have issues, either ‘Warning’ or ‘Error’. The Error message will
be automatically generated, if the custom "Error Message" is left blank in the survey designing phase.

The erroneous records can be directly accessed and edited from the Validation Report view.

Click a row (or its edit icon) to open the record. Click the arrows next to Path, Messages and Owner to sort
the report. Use the buttons above the table to show only part of the messages:

•  Filter attributes: show only the messages of the selected attributes.

•  Filter messages: show only the selected message types (Required value, Invalid value, Duplicate
value, Duplicate entity key, Duplicate record key, Node count, Custom validation).

•  Filter records: show only the records matching an expression, written in JavaScript syntax as in Data
Explorer (see 9.6.1), e.g. cluster_id <= 5.

The filters are also applied when exporting the report.

The validation report can be exported into an Excel file by clicking on the  button.
The report contains more information than the screen view, and it looks in MS Excel as follows.

sections.title: Merging data (1/2)
sections.text:
Records can be merged into one. This feature works only when it's applied to 2 records at a time.

Select the 2 records to merge in the records list (Data → Records), then press the Merge button on the top
bar.

Merging data can be quite useful when, for example, data on the same site is collected using different
devices; Arena and Arena Mobile don't allow creating records with the same identifiers (keys), but to make
the data collection in the field faster, users can work on the same site (cluster) with different devices and
combine the data later on. (e.g. when you have a survey with a structure cluster -> plot -> tree, users in the
same cluster can collect tree data in different sample plots).

The survey must be prepared in a way that makes merging records easier.

During the merge process, the newer record will be considered as "source", while the older one as "target",
so that values in the source record will go into the target record.

The merging process goes through every "entity" in the record, starting from the root.

-  entities with the same key attribute values will be "merged";
-  entities in the source record but not in the target one will be added;
-  entities on the target record but not on the source one will be kept;
-  attributes with values in the target record will not be replaced by values of the source record;
-  empty attributes in the target record will be replaced with the ones in the source record;

A simple way to allow merging records is to start collecting data with one device, then on another device only
the key attributes of the entities could be filled, and other attributes can be skipped/left blank. Here is an
example of how 2 records will be merged; in this case, the survey has a quite simple structure such as cluster
-> plot -> tree; the target record has 1 plot with 2 trees, the source record has a plot with the same ID as the
target record and 1 tree with an ID different from the ones of the trees in the target record plot; the expected
result is to have the "new" tree inside the target record plot, like this:

target record, also the "new" plot will be added to the target record, like in this example:

Before applying for the merge, a preview of the results will be shown and the user will have to confirm the

record will be modified, adding value from the source record.

When 2 records have too many differences from each other, a warning message will be shown to the user;
in that case, the user could have selected 2 records that are not compatible for the merge.

sections.title: Merging data (2/2)
sections.text:
Merging records with the same keys

Records with the same key attribute values can come from different Arena Mobile devices, or from Arena
files imported with the Merge records conflict resolution strategy. When they are uploaded or imported
with the merge option, they are merged into the existing record instead of being duplicated (merging
follows the rules described above).

This is allowed by default. To prevent it, go to Home → Survey Info → Security, unselect Allow merging
records with same keys (e.g. records created in different Arena Mobile devices) and click Save. When the
option is not selected, importing a record with the same keys as an existing one stops with an error.

sections.title: Exporting a printable document
sections.text:
To export a printable document of a record, follow the next steps:

1. Open a record in Data → Records.

2. Navigate to the page you want to print. This is only needed when printing the current page.
3. Click the PDF icon (Export Document) in the record header bar.
4. In the "Export printable document" dialog, select the options and click Download.

Option  Explanation

Format  PDF or Word (.docx). The Word file can be edited further before printing.

Content  Full survey: the whole record, with the survey label and description as the title.
Current page only: only the entity instance currently shown in the form (e.g. the
plot or tree you are viewing), with the entity label as the title. Its subpages are
not included.

Include QR code  Adds a QR code to the first page. Available only with "Current page only".

Page orientation  Portrait or Landscape. The selection will be the document default. Entities with
their own orientation set in the Print tab override it.

The document is generated in the language currently selected in the form's language selector, and for the
cycle of the record. The downloaded file is named after the survey, the cycle and, for "Current page only",
the entity label.

Note: "Current page only" requires a specific entity instance to be open. If the current page belongs to a
multiple entity and no row or form is selected, the dialog shows a message. In that case, navigate to a specific
instance or export the full survey.

What is included in the document

●  The layout follows the Form Designer. Attributes are placed according to the form grid (columns and
positions). Multiple entities displayed as tables are printed as tables. Multiple entities displayed as
forms are printed once per instance, each under its own heading.
●  Entities on their own page, and multiple entities at the upper levels of the hierarchy, start on a new
page.
●  Code attributes show the item label. Taxon attributes show the scientific name followed by the code.
●  Boolean attributes use the label value set in the attribute (Yes/No or True/False).
●  Image file attributes are printed as pictures. Other file types show the file name.
●  Attributes set as Hide in entry form, and nodes that are not relevant or not visible in the record, are
not printed.
●  Calculated result attributes from processing chains are not included.

Example of a printed page (current page only, with QR code):

sections.title: QR code
sections.text:
When the "Include QR code" option is enabled, Arena stores a read-only PDF copy of the exported page on
the server and prints a QR code in the top-right corner of the first page. Scanning the QR code with any
smartphone opens the stored PDF.

●  The link is valid for one year.
●  Exporting the same page again with the QR code option updates the stored PDF with the current
data and extends the validity by another year. The QR code and its link remain unchanged, ensuring
that previously printed copies continue to work.
●  The QR link can be accessed without logging in to Arena. Anyone who has the printed document can
view that page's data. Therefore, carefully consider whether to use this feature for records
containing personal, confidential, or otherwise sensitive information.

sections.title: Creating a processing chain (1/2)
sections.text:
Data processing in Arena is implemented using R scripts. Each survey has its own set of scripts, which can be
created and modified by the Survey Administrator or Data Analyst. The processing can be executed either in
a cloud-based RStudio environment or locally using R and RStudio installed on a personal computer, which is
the recommended approach.

Data processing is carried out through a calculation chain consisting of the result variables to be calculated.
Each computation within the chain is referred to in this manual as a calculation step. While a survey can
contain several calculation chains, only one chain can be designated for applying the Sampling Design and
Statistical Analysis methods.

Advantages of the processing chain

●  Automated calculation result attributes (e.g., tree volume, biomass, carbon),
●  One script – it is transparent and easy to repeat,
●  R provides powerful statistical engine,
●  Efficiency and reproducibility of inventory workflows by standardizing processing steps,
●  Provides a foundation for reporting and documentation.

The concept of using a data processing chain in sampling-based assessment is illustrated in the following
chart.

Chains are common across all cycles. If the user needs to apply different data processing rules by cycles, this
needs to be taken into account inside the R scripts.

Start creating a new calculation chain by clicking  button.

Then give the calculation chain information.

Input fields

-  Processing chain label  * name for the chain (required),
-  Description  * descriptive text about the chain (optional),
-  Sampling Design  * enable if you have sampling-based data (only one chain per
survey); the Sampling Design tab is then shown,
-  Records  * number of records on different steps (of the selected cycle)

By default, the form of an existing processing chain is locked (a chain you have just created stays unlocked).
Use  these  two  buttons  to  unlock/lock  the  form.

RStudio options (expand the RStudio panel of the Basic tab)

1) If enabled, only the analysis stage data will be copied
to the RStudio session.

2) Only selected records’ data are submitted to the
RStudio session.

3) Enable this option if the result variables are read back
into the Arena server from the RStudio session with
[system/persist-results.R]

A chain must contain at least one calculation step, represented by a result variable. You can add either a
quantitative (numeric) variable or a categorical (coded) variable.

For example, tree stem volume is a quantitative variable.

First, click the  button.

Then, select the entity name from the dropdown list.

Then fill in the variable’s name 12, label (optional), unit (optional), and number of decimal digits (optional,
used in Data Explorer only). The variable names must be unique in a survey.

Select  if you want to compute area-based results for the given variable, such
as "volume per hectare" or "number of trees per hectare".

In the Statistical Analysis with a Shiny app, we can only report the area-based variables.

IMPORTANT: Follow these steps while renaming an area-based result variable

1) disable "area-based estimate" and approve to delete the node, 13
2) rename your result variable, and
3) enable  back active again

R scripts can only be created and edited in RStudio. In Arena, they can be viewed but not modified. Click Save
& Back to return to the previous screen.

12 If you are working with forest inventory data, please see the recommended naming approach in "Naming of
entities & attributes: Recommendations" under “Arena” at https://www.openforis.org/support-and-resources/

13 The reason for doing this is that when you disable the checkbox, the system will delete an internal
"variablename_ha" attribute from the database. When you enable it, the system will create a new attribute
"newname_ha" into the database.

You will see the list of results variables as follows.

sections.title: Creating a processing chain (2/2)
sections.text:
Note 1: In the label text, the suffix (C) means that this is a calculated (chain) attribute.

Note 2: After saving a result variable, its properties can be edited but the parent entity cannot be changed.

Note 3: When you edit an existing result variable, use the arrow buttons at the bottom of the page to move
to the previous or next result variable of the chain, Back to return to the chain, and Delete to delete the
variable.

ACTIVE/DEACTIVATE variable button: This method allows users to include or exclude a result
variable in the data processing in R.

Note: if you have earlier processed your results with an "area-based" result variable that you want
to deactivate, the results per hectare ("_ha") will still emerge in the Data Explorer and in the
CSV/Excel export data. If you want to remove this "per hectare" attribute, first deselect "area-based
estimate" in the attribute’s properties page, and then deactivate that attribute. Then run the analysis
chain one more time in RStudio.

Categorical result variables are used for data aggregation and reporting. Click the

R scripts can be created, debugged, and run in RStudio. An overview of the entire processing chain is provided

The following two options are available for using RStudio with Arena:

1)  Use RStudio Server in the cloud, or

2)  Use locally installed RStudio (in your machine).

To run RStudio locally, ensure that:

●  R version 4.1.3 or newer is installed.
●  The rstudioapi package is installed.
●  An active internet connection is available.
●  You start a new RStudio session.

The workflow for both RStudio options is as follows:

1) Publish the survey. This step is required whenever changes have been made to the survey structure,
survey data, or calculation chain.

2) Select whether you want to submit all data or only analysis step data to RStudio.

Note: For multi-cycle surveys, only the data from the currently selected cycle will be submitted to
RStudio.

3) Click the RStudio Remote (RStudio Server) or RStudio Local button in the RStudio panel to start the
process.
Note: The RStudio process cannot be started if no data are available for submission (i.e. all record
counts are zero).

4) The following message will be displayed. The message differs slightly depending on whether you are
using the server-based or local RStudio environment:

Click OK to continue.

Arena will automatically copy the initialization script to your clipboard 14.

5) RStudio Server: RStudio will open automatically.

14 The initialization script is valid for 60 minutes, and after that it will expire.

Local RStudio: Start RStudio on your computer.

6) Paste the copied script into the RStudio Console (Ctrl+V) and execute it. This step uploads all survey
scripts from Arena's PostgreSQL database to RStudio.

7) In the Files pane, the following structure will be available 15

arena.R  =  Main  program  file  (do  not  edit!).
system/  = Directory containing system-generated files (do not edit!).
sampling/ = Directory containing scripts for base-unit weights and plot areas (can be edited).
user/  = Directory containing scripts for result variables, one file per variable numbered in chain

of R packages required by Arena into the current RStudio session. In Local RStudio, only a small set
of essential packages is installed, and only if they are not already available 16.

15 When using local RStudio in a Windows machine, the files are downloaded into the following folder:
C:\Users\USERNAME\Documents\arena

16 The list of required R packages can be found at /system/init/init-packages.R

The complete list of packages used by Arena can be found in: system/init/init-packages.R

The following data will be added into the R project:

●  Data from all entities included in the calculation chain.
●  Data from the Base Unit and Clustering entities.
●  All categorical and taxonomic tables, stored as lists of data frames.
●  The schema summary table (arena.schemaSummary).
●  The chain summary object (arena.chainSummary), which contains information about the
structure and content of the calculation chain.

10) Once the data have been loaded successfully, open the user/ folder to access the scripts associated
with the survey's result variables.

This folder contains the common file for adding R scripts (as functions) that are common for all
calculation steps following file 000-common.R

Important: about using R packages

●  Whenever possible, load all your required packages in 000-common.R, as this
provides a single location for managing package dependencies and simplifies
script maintenance.

●  Note that RStudio Server runs on a Linux environment. As a result, some R
packages that are available on other operating systems may not work on the
server.

●  When using additional packages, avoid loading them with the library() function.
Instead, use the usePackage() function, for example:
usePackage("lmfor")

The usePackage() function checks whether the specified package is already
installed. If the package is not available, it is installed automatically. The function
is defined in the system file init-packages.R:

●  Since a large number of packages may be loaded during an RStudio session, it is

recommended to explicitly qualify function names with their package names to
avoid conflicts. For example:

dplyr::select(),  dplyr::filter()
This practice improves code readability and helps ensure that the intended
function is used when multiple packages provide functions with the same name.

11) The scripts located in the user/ and sampling/ folders are the primary files that require user-
developed code.

Within the RStudio project, survey data are organized into data frames corresponding to each entity.
In addition, two lists of data frames are available: categories and taxonomies.
For example, if the survey includes a code list named land_use, it can be accessed as
categories$land_use.

Taxonomic tables may also contain additional attributes, such as species-specific wood density
values. Since these attributes are stored as character fields in Arena, they must be converted to
numeric data types before being used in calculations.

12) Once all scripts have been tested, saved, and executed without errors, run the main program by
opening arena.R and clicking the Source button.

This process uploads all updated R scripts and writes the computed results back to the Arena
database. If the calculation chain includes Sampling Design and Statistical Analysis settings, the
resulting output tables will also be exported as CSV files (see Chapter 10.4.4 for details).

13) RStudio Server users: After the processing has completed successfully, close your RStudio session by

Terminating the connection frees server resources and makes them available to other users of the
cloud-based RStudio service.

If RStudio Server does not start

In such cases, please wait 5 to 10 minutes and try again. This issue may occur when many users are attempting

Working with external files (e.g. CSVs and image files)

sections.title: RStudio in programming and data processing (3/3)
sections.text:
In arena.R, each module invocation within the processing chain includes an argument for capturing and
handling errors, as illustrated in the example below.

All errors encountered during script execution are collected in a global error log. This log is evaluated by the
script system/persist-user-scripts.R when user-developed R scripts are saved back to the Arena server. If any
errors are present in the log, execution of the calculation chain is halted and a warning message is displayed
in the R Console. All reported errors must be resolved before the chain can be executed successfully.

After fixing the erroneous R code, the error log must be cleared before rerunning the scripts. There are three
ways to do this:

1) Restart  the  chain  from  system/init.R.
This clears the error log automatically. However, the survey data needs to be reloaded from the
Arena server into RStudio, which may take considerable time for large datasets.
2) Run  cleanGlobalErrors()  in  the  R  Console.
After clearing the error log, rerun the chain starting from the corrected script or module.
3) Add  cleanGlobalErrors()  to  000-common.R.
By including this command in 000-common.R, the error log will be cleared automatically when you
rerun the chain from that point.

Choosing the second or third option is often more efficient, as it avoids reloading data from the server and
reduces processing time during script development and testing.

Problems with system/persist-results.R

IIn some cases, computed results cannot be written back to the Arena database. One common cause is the
presence of one or more data frame columns that contain only NA values. When this occurs, error messages
similar to the examples below may be displayed.

Or the error message is this one:

The first step is to inspect the result variables and verify whether any of them contain only NA values. If all
result variables appear valid, the issue may originate from the input data retrieved from Arena.

A practical solution is to remove any columns that consist entirely of missing values before rerunning the
result persistence process. For example, if the error occurs in the tree data frame, the following command
removes all columns whose values are exclusively NA:

tree[sapply(tree, function(x) all(is.na(x)))] <- NULL

After removing the affected columns, rerun the system/persist-results.R script to write the results back to the
Arena database.

Viewing updated scripts in Arena

User scripts are saved back to the Arena database by the system/persist-user-scripts.R script.

If an updated script is not immediately visible in the Arena script editor, refresh your web browser to reload
the latest version from the database.

sections.title: About computing area-based variables
sections.text:
In most forest inventory projects, results are typically reported by area units. In contrast, area-based
estimates are generally not required for activities such as interviews and socio-economic surveys.

When you create a result variable and enable the Area-based estimate option, Arena automatically creates
a corresponding variable in the database (for example, tree_volume becomes tree_volume_ha).

In Arena, all variables generated by the processing chain can be displayed by enabling

17 You need to PUBLISH the survey in order to enable this button.

In the RStudio project, a new sampling folder is created containing additional files used for sampling-based
estimation, as described in the following sections.

The sampling/ folder contains scripts for calculating base-unit weights and the sampling areas required for
area-based result variables.

Depending on the survey design, base-unit weights can be defined in different ways. For example, all sample
plots may be assigned equal weights, while inaccessible plots can be assigned a weight of zero and excluded
from the estimation process.

All plots get equal weights:  Inaccessible plots get no weights:

corresponding sampling script.

Note: The name of a plot-area variable always includes a prefix derived from the entity name, such as
tree_plot_area_ or bamboo_plot_area_.

Arena automatically generates additional code in system/calculate-results.R to convert area-based
measurements into per-hectare (or per-acre) results:

After the full processing chain has been executed successfully in RStudio, all user-developed scripts are saved
back to the Arena server. If the “Results Read Back from RStudio” option is enabled, the computed result
variables are also written back to the Arena database.

These result variables can then be viewed, explored, and aggregated using the Arena Explorer tool. The figure
below illustrates how area-based result variables are displayed in both the Explorer view and the Hierarchy view.

Variables marked with (C) are computed variables, indicating that their values are generated through the
calculation chain rather than entered directly by users’ input data.

Weight and plot area attributes

When the chain has a base unit (see the Sampling Design tab), Arena creates the following sampling
attributes every time you publish the survey:

•  weight, in the base unit entity (default script: plot$weight <- 1);

•  <entity>_plot_area_ (e.g. tree_plot_area_), in every entity with an active area-based result variable
of the chain (default script: tree$tree_plot_area_ <- NA: replace NA with the plot area formula).

These decimal attributes are not shown in the data entry forms and cannot be deactivated. Arena deletes
them when they are no longer needed, for example when the base unit changes or an entity has no active
area-based result variables anymore. Their scripts are in the sampling/ folder of the RStudio project (the
weight first). To see them in the list of result variables, select Show sampling attributes:

sections.title: Sampling strategy
sections.text:
This section will cover defining a sample strategy in Arena. A sample strategy is the combination of sample
design along with an estimator (formula) from which is calculated an estimate for a parameter of interest.
For many strategies the sample design and formula are so closely associated that the term "design" is used
when "strategy" is meant, we will follow this convention.

Arena supports the following sampling strategies: 1) simple random sampling and systematic sampling;
2) stratified sampling; and 3) single stage or cluster sampling. In addition, the script can compute area
estimates for 4) two-phase sampling (UNDER DEVELOPMENT, non-clustered, or clustered).

Definitions and Background

Most forest inventory measurement protocols use a set of circles or rectangles; the set is arranged
geometrically around the sample point for the set, see figure below.

In a majority of inventories, the set is referred to as a cluster and individual elements are referred to as plots.
One exception is the Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) program of the United States Forest Service, which
refers to the set as a plot and individual elements as subplots. To avoid confusion between the two uses of
"plot" we will refer to the FIA set as the FIA-plot.

In Open Foris Calc, the smallest unit of measured area is called a base unit, and it is assumed that the base
unit is of a single stand type. For many inventories the plot is the base unit. Although in some inventories the
plot can be mapped into different stand types. One example of this is FIA, which has the field crews divide
the subplots into different stands if there is a stand boundary which can be repeatable mapped.

Typically, trees are measured on clusters of plots, where the plots may vary in size and/or number depending
on the diameter class of the tree. Therefore, each entity that contains "area-based" variable(s) gets a new
result attribute automatically in a processing chain, for example "tree" gets attribute "tree_plot_area_".

Areas of strata

Stratified sampling requires computation of inclusion probabilities by stratum. In Arena, inclusion
probabilities are expressed as "expansion factors" (which are equal to the inverse of inclusion probability).

There are two methods in Arena script to compute expansion factor for a base unit:

a) Computation  with  the  help  of  sample  weights  in  stratum,  i.e.
Exp_factor = [base unit weight in stratum] / (sum([base unit weights in stratum])
b) Areas  of  stratum  is  known,  i.e.
Exp_factor = [area in stratum] / (sum([base unit weights in stratum])

Method A does not allow you to compute "Totals" (such as total volume, biomass) correctly. However, per
hectare results can be computed.

In case B, sampling areas must be provided. These are given via the category table of the stratification entity,
in  a  column  named  "area".  All  areas  are  given  in  hectares  (or  acres).

sections.title: Non-response bias corrections
sections.text:
A problem common to nearly all sample-based surveys is partial or complete non-response from some of the
selected sample units. Arena script can apply the Weighting Class Adjustment method and compute weight
adjustment factors based on data about the planned number of sampling units. In this case, missing
observations are ignored and an adjustment factor is incorporated into a sample weight to compensate for
non-response or situations where all or part of a sample (plot) falls outside the population.

The weight adjustment requires information about the planned number of Primary Sampling Units (PSUs)
and Secondary Sampling Units (SSUs).

In a forest inventory, Primary Sampling Units can be sample plots or clusters, by strata in case of stratified
sampling. Secondary Sampling Units can be sample plots.

sections.title: Arenalytics - R package for statistical analysis and reporting (1/2)
sections.text:
Arenalytics is an analytical dashboard developed for reporting and exploring data collected and processed
with Open Foris Arena. It was designed to address one of the main challenges of sample-based assessments:
generating reliable statistics, tables, and figures from large and complex survey datasets without requiring
users to predefine all reporting outputs in advance. The dashboard was developed particularly for forest

inventories and other sample-based assessments where users need to produce estimates such as biomass,
tree density, volume, carbon stocks, or other indicators across multiple reporting domains. The dashboard
allows users to dynamically analyse survey results by selecting measures, dimensions, and filters, producing
estimates, totals, means, and reliability statistics on demand.

The Arenalytics workflow begins in Open Foris Arena, where survey data are collected and processed using a
calculation chain. Once the processing chain has been executed in RStudio, Arena automatically generates
Minimum Area Unit (MAU) files that contain pre-computed result variables and supporting attributes
required for reporting. These files are packaged into a ZIP archive and loaded into Arenalytics for analysis.

After loading a MAU zip file, Arenalytics performs automatic validation checks and provides a survey
summary to help users verify that the uploaded data are ready for analysis. Users can then select an entity,
choose one or more measures to analyse, and define dimensions and filters that determine how results will
be aggregated and presented. Dimensions can originate from either the original survey data or from the
processing chain, enabling flexible reporting across administrative units, forest types, diameter classes,
species groups, and many other categories. The resulting tables are generated instantly and updated
whenever  the  settings  in  the  ‘Cross  outputs  settings’  section  change.

Workflow Summary:

Arena Survey with Data and Processing Chain
→ Run Chain in RStudio
→ Generate MAU ZIP file
→ Load data into Arenalytics

→ Select Entity and Dimensions

→ Click Run analysis
→ Select Measures and Filters
→ Review & Export results
→ Create figures
→ Generate reports

The dashboard can be accessed through a web application or installed locally from its open-source R package,
making it suitable for both online and offline environments:

1. Use the online version. Open the hosted dashboard in your web browser: https://openforis-
shiny.shinyapps.io/arenalytics/
2. RECOMMENDED: Install and run locally in a Rstudio instance with

if (!require(remotes)) install.packages("remotes")

if (!require(arenalytics)) remotes::install_github("openforis/arenalytics",
upgrade="never")

arenalytics::shiny_run_arenalytics()

The internal showcase presentation also notes that a demo dataset is available in the About section of the

application. A step-by-step guideline to Arenalytics is available here.

The outcome of the Arena processing chain is a ZIP file of semi-aggregated data that will serve as input for
Arenalytics, a Minimum Area Unit (MAU) file. The MAU file contains data aggregated to the Minimum Area
Unit level, which is defined as the smallest homogeneous land unit in the survey area. In the Arena processing
chain, the MAU is equivalent to the base unit used for statistical estimation.

Examples:

●  If a plot is completely homogeneous (single land use or vegetation type), the plot itself is the MAU.
●  If a plot is divided into several land-use or vegetation sections, then each homogeneous section
becomes a separate MAU unit. Estimation variables are first computed for these sections and then
aggregated to higher reporting levels.

The MAU file is automatically generated by an Arena system script as a ZIP file. It contains:

●  Result estimates for each base unit (MAU).
●  All relevant dimensions derived from categorical, taxonomic, and Boolean attributes.

sections.title: Arenalytics - R package for statistical analysis and reporting (2/2)
sections.text:
●  Pre-computed measures that Arenalytics can subsequently aggregate into tables, charts, means,
totals, and sampling-error estimates for any user-selected combination of dimensions.

Arenalytics reads measures at the MAU level and dynamically aggregates them to any reporting level (forest
type, species, administrative region, diameter class, etc.) requested by the user. For a typical forest inventory
case, where plots may be split into land-use strata or forest types, you can think of the MAU file as a dataset
where each record represents one homogeneous plot section together with all its computed area-based
variables and reporting dimensions.

The generated MAU ZIP file can be stored on the Arena server to facilitate archiving and future retrieval.
Follow these steps:

1. Unlock the chain
2. Click Advanced functions and then Upload MAU.zip

3. Once the file is uploaded, you will see an option to download or delete this file:

The MAU.zip file is linked to the cycle selected in the header: if the survey has more than one cycle, Arena
asks you to confirm the cycle before uploading the file, and Download MAU.zip and Delete MAU.zip work
on the file of the current cycle.

Only .zip files are accepted. If a MAU.zip file has already been uploaded for the chain, Arena asks you to
confirm before replacing it. Upload MAU.zip and Delete MAU.zip are available only when the chain is
unlocked, Download MAU.zip also when it is locked.

sections.title: Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
This chapter explains how to copy an existing processing chain with R scripts from one survey into another
without rebuilding a new chain step by step.

sections.title: Overview
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
The ‘Clone chain from another survey’ feature lets a Survey Administrator or Data Analyst copy a complete
chain from a survey they have access to into the survey they are currently working on. The clone operation
copies:

●  the chain's properties (name, labels, and description);
●  all R scripts;
●  the calculated result variables (analysis attributes) defined in the chain, re-created under the
matching entities of the destination survey;
●  the categories and taxonomies referenced by those calculated variables, so that coded results keep
working after the clone.

The cloned chain is created as a new, independent chain in the destination survey - the source chain is left
untouched, and the two chains are not kept in sync after cloning.

sections.title: Prerequisites
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
● You must have Survey Administrator or Data Analyst permissions in the destination survey (the one
you want to copy the chain into).
● You must also have access to the source survey (the one the chain is copied from). Only surveys you
can access, and that already contain at least one chain, are offered as a source.
● The destination survey should already contain the entities that the source chain's calculated variables
refer to (for example, plot or tree), using the same entity names. Arena checks this for you before
the clone runs; if the entities do not exist in the target survey, the analysis variables associated to
those entities won’t be cloned.

sections.title: Step-by-step: cloning a chain
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
1. Open the destination survey (the survey you want the chain copied into) and go to Analysis → Chains.
2. In the Chains panel, click the button “Clone from another survey”.
3. In the Clone chain from another survey dialog, select the Source survey (or template) from the
dropdown list. Only surveys and templates you have access to, and that contain at least one chain,
appear here.
4. Select the Source chain you want to copy from the list of chains available in that survey.
5. Arena automatically runs a compatibility check, comparing the entities used by the source chain's
calculation steps with the entities available in the destination survey.

6. Review the compatibility results. If everything is compatible, confirm the clone by clicking Clone.
Entities that do not exist in the destination survey are marked as missing in target survey: select Skip
analysis attributes for entities missing in the target survey to clone the chain without their analysis
attributes (otherwise Clone stays disabled).
7. Arena creates the new chain in the destination survey, copies the scripts and calculated variables,
and then opens the newly created chain automatically so you can review it.

sections.title: What happens after cloning
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
●  A new chain is created in the destination survey with a new, unique identifier, it is entirely separate
from the source chain.
●  All R scripts from the source chain are copied over as-is; you can edit them afterwards like any other
chain script.
●  Calculated variables are re-created under the matching entities of the destination survey, together
with any categories or taxonomies they depend on.
●  The new chain is validated automatically once created, and any issues (for example, an expression
referencing an attribute that does not exist in the destination survey) are flagged for you to resolve,
the same way validation works for a chain you build manually.
●  You are  taken directly to the newly created chain, ready for review, adjustment, and
publishing.

sections.title: Notes and limitations
path: 10.6. Duplicate or clone a chain from another survey
sections.text:
● Cloning copies the chain definition and scripts; it does not copy previously computed results or
published data — you still need to run the chain in RStudio to generate results in the destination
survey.
● Only chains you can access (i.e., chains belonging to surveys you are a member of, or to published
templates) can be used as a source.
● If the source and destination surveys use different names for otherwise equivalent entities, rename
the entity in one of the two surveys first so the compatibility check can match them.
● A survey can contain more than one chain; cloning adds a new chain alongside any chains that already
exist in the destination survey; it does not replace them.

•  When you clone a whole survey (Clone in the new survey page), its chains are cloned too.

sections.title: Deleting a chain
sections.text:
A calculation chain can be deleted from the Advanced functions menu. Unlock the form and click Delete
chain.

This action cannot be canceled.

sections.title: User roles and invitation to access a survey
User roles

sections.title: Invitation to survey
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
A Survey Administrator can invite new users to get access to the current published survey.

To send an invitation to a new survey user or a group of users, go to the  section and

click the  button. The following form will appear.

The invitation is sent to all set email addresses. Fill in first the email addresses (type each address and press
Add), then select a Role, and type an additional message, if needed. The Permissions of the selected role are

This is an example of email that the client will get:

The text of the message is shorter if the invited person (i.e. email) is already a registered Arena user.

If a recipient does not get an email, the message might be blocked by a strict firewall filter on the recipient’s
