sections.title: User Grouping
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey

sections.title: Overview
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
A Survey Administrator can organize the people who collect data for a survey into named groups (e.g., by
region, team, or organization). A group can optionally carry one or more qualifiers (key/value pairs that
automatically restrict and pre-fill the data that its members collect) so that each group only can see and edit
the records that belong to them.

User Groups are useful when:

● Several field teams share the same survey but should not see or edit each other’s records.
● Records must be automatically tagged with a region, project, or organization code as soon as they are
created, based on who is entering the data.
● You want to get a quick overview of which users are assigned to which team, and a method to reassign
them.

sections.title: Accessing User Groups
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
Only users with a Survey Administrator role in the current survey can create, edit, delete groups, or manage
members.

User Groups are managed per survey, via the Users section of the survey menu:

1. Select the survey and go to Users on the left-hand side menu.
2. Select the User Groups tab.

The User Groups page has up to three tabs, depending on your permissions:

Tab  What it shows

User Groups  A simple list of the groups defined in the survey.

Group Assignments  A Kanban-style board with one column per group (plus an "Unassigned" column) and
one card per user; drag and drop a user’s card to change their group.

Members Report  A flat table with one row per group member, listing the group’s name, label and
qualifiers alongside the member’s name, email, survey role and account status.

sections.title: Creating and Editing a User Group
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
1. On the User Groups tab, click New Group.
2. Enter a Name for the group. The name is normalized automatically (no spaces or special characters) and
it must be unique within the survey.
3. Enter a Label for each survey language – this is the friendly name shown to users throughout Arena.
4. Optionally add one or more Qualifiers (see 11.3.4) and select in Can view the records of the groups whose
records the members can view (see 11.3.8).
5. Click Save. Once the group is saved, a Members panel appears at the bottom of the page (see 11.3.5).

To edit an existing group, open it from the User Groups list and change any field, then click Save again. To
remove a group, open it and click Delete; in this case the members are not deleted, they simply become
unassigned.

sections.title: Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
A qualifier is a key/value pair attached to a group. The key must match the name of a survey attribute that
has been marked as a qualifier attribute in the Form Designer (see 11.3.4.1). When this is done, Arena uses
the pair to automatically fill in and restrict data for members of that group.

sections.title: Marking an attribute as a Qualifier
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
Only single-value Text or Code attributes placed directly under the root entity of the form can be used as
qualifiers. To enable one, do next:

1.  Open the Form Designer and select the text or code attribute (it must be defined inside the root level
entity) that will hold the group value (for example, "region" or "project_code").

2.  In the attribute’s Basic Properties panel, enable the Qualifier checkbox. This option only appears once
when at least one User Group exists in the survey.

What "Qualifier" does: When a new record is created by a user belonging to a group, this attribute is
automatically filled with the value specified for it among that group’s qualifiers. Users will only be able to see and
modify records belonging to their own group if they belong to one.

sections.title: Adding qualifier values to a group
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
Back on the group’s edit page, in the Qualifiers panel:

1. Click Add qualifier.
2. Under Key, enter the exact name of the qualifier attribute defined on the form (e.g. "region").
3. Under Value, enter the value that should apply to this group (e.g. "North"; for a Code attribute, enter the
item’s code).
4. Repeat for additional qualifier attributes, and then click Save.

A group can have several qualifiers if the form defines several qualifier attributes. Each qualifier key must be
unique within the group, and it cannot be left blank.

sections.title: Effect on data entry and data access
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
11.3.4. Qualifiers: Linking a Group to Survey Data
sections.text:
● New record: the qualifier attribute(s) are filled in automatically as soon as a member of the group starts
collecting a new record, using the value(s) set on their group.
● Existing records: a user can only view and edit records whose qualifier attribute value matches their own
group’s qualifier value. Attempts to open or edit a record outside their group are rejected.
● Unassigned users, or groups without a matching qualifier, are not restricted by this mechanism.
● Guests: the members of the group with the Guest role can view the records of their group (and of the
groups selected in Can view the records of, see 11.3.8), also in Arena Mobile, but they cannot edit them,
nor add new records.
● A user is considered to belong to at most one group per survey; only that group’s qualifiers are applied.

sections.title: Managing Group Members
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text: There are two ways to assign survey users to a group. These are explained next.

sections.title: Method 1. From the group’s edit page
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
1. Open the group and scroll to the Members panel.
2. Use the Add member dropdown to pick up a survey user by name and email.
3. If the chosen user already belongs to a different group, Arena asks for confirmation before moving them
(a user can only be a member of one group at a time).
4. To remove a member, click the ✕ icon next to their name. They become unassigned, not deleted from
the survey.

sections.title: Method 2. From the Group Assignments board (drag and drop)
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
The Group Assignments tab (visible only to users who can manage groups) shows every survey user as a card
on a Kanban-style board, with one column per group plus a leading Unassigned column.

1.  Go to Users > User Groups > Group Assignments.
2.  Drag a user’s card from its current column into the column of the group you want to assign them to (or
into Unassigned to remove them from any group).

The new status is saved immediately; there is no separate Save step for this view.

sections.title: Members Report
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
The Members Report tab gives a flat, exportable-style view for auditing group membership: one row per
group/member pair, showing the group’s name, label and qualifiers next to the member’s name, email,
survey role and account status (Invited, Accepted, or Password change required). Groups with no members
still appear, with a single empty-member row, so no group is missed.

sections.title: Frequently Asked Questions
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
● Can a user belong to more than one group?
No. Adding a user to a group who already belongs to a different group moves them to the new group
after a confirmation prompt.

● What happens to a group’s members if the group is deleted?
They are not removed from the survey; they simply become unassigned and lose any qualifier
restriction that the group applied.

● Can I use a multiple-choice or nested attribute as a qualifier?
No. Only single-value Text or Code attributes placed directly under the root entity of the form can be
marked as qualifiers.

sections.title: Read-only access to the records of other groups
path: 11. User roles and invitation to access a survey
sections.text:
The members of a group with qualifiers can see and edit only the records of their own group. To let them
also view the records of other groups (e.g. a supervisors' team), open the group and select those groups in
Can view the records of, then click Save.

The members of the group can then view, export and download (also in Arena Mobile) the records of the
selected groups, but they cannot edit them. In the example of section 11.3.3, the members of the
Morogoro team can view the records of the Arusha team.

Record files, data exports and the records uploaded from Arena Mobile are also restricted to the records
that the user group can access.

sections.title: Examples of expressions
sections.text:
Arena uses Javascript programming language for expressions. Because some users may be familiar with XPath language expressions used in OF Collect, the
tables (use the link below) represent expressions with both these languages.

The filters of the Data Explorer and of the Validation report also use JavaScript syntax only. To search text values use includes, startsWith or endsWith, e.g.
remarks.includes('dead'); add .toLowerCase() before them to ignore the case, e.g. remarks.toLowerCase().includes('dead').

Note: In JavaScript, a string is a sequence of characters enclosed in single (‘) or double (") quotes. The choice of quoting style is up to the programmer.

Operands (see more here):
AND: &&  OR : ||  NOT: !
Equal to: ==  not equal: !=  Less than: <, <=  Greater than: >, >=
Multiplication: * , Division: / , Modulo: % , Exponentiation: **

All examples of expressions you can find in this online document. It contains the following topics:

12.1. "Relevant if" and "Apply if" rules
12.2. Methods and functions
12.3. Data validation
12.4. Functions using current user
12.5. Functions using current record
12.6. Examples
12.7. Items filter expressions

How to avoid performance issues with Arena / Arena Mobile

If you encounter slowness while editing a large number of entities in a multiple entity (table), you should check the expressions set in for every attribute
(default values, validation rules, etc.), because, depending on the way they are defined, they can be evaluated by Arena and Arena Mobile too many times.
This can happen when you record a new entity or delete an existing one.

Please follow these rules:

●  when you have a default value with an expression that depends on the "index" of the entity, like index($context) + 1, mark it with "Default value
evaluated only one time", otherwise the expression will be evaluated repeatedly every time you insert a new entity;
●  when you have a validation rule that checks the value of an attribute, please prefer the use of " this" instead of the name of the variable; e.g.
this > 10 instead of attribute_name > 10 or parent_entity_name.attribute_name > 10
●  When you point at another attribute (e.g. this < tree_height_top), make sure that the attribute (tree_height_top) precedes in the data structure.

sections.title: System administration
Backup and restore users
sections.text:
You can copy the users from one Arena server to another one. In Users list (all), click Backup / Restore:

•  Backup users exports the users with their survey roles and user groups (2FA devices are not
exported). Choose which users to export: All users, the Selected users (select them with the
checkbox in the first column of the list: the selection is kept when changing page or searching) or the
Users with these emails (type or paste the email addresses, one per line or separated by commas).

user groups are matched by survey name and group name, and the roles of surveys not existing in

backup. If the passwords are not included in the backup, new users will have to reset their password.

sections.title: System architecture
sections.text:
OF Arena is built with JavaScript programming language and the system is based on the following
components:

•  Static front-end in React.js

•  Back-end in Node.js

•  Database Management System: PostgreSQL

•  Amazon Web Services (AWS),

•  Leaflet JavaScript library for interactive maps,

•  System front-end and back-end will communicate via Web Socket connection, and the OF Arena
authentication system uses local user storage. OF Arena sends notifications via email.

•  External data: users can upload files into the system,

•  OF Arena integrates with RStudio server,

•  Local off-line installation and usage via docker.

OF Arena uses cookies, so they should be allowed in the web browser. The system is tested with the following
web browsers: Google Chrome (recommended), Windows Edge and Opera.

sections.title: RStudio Server: writing and downloading files created during run-time
sections.text:
Because RStudio Server works on a remote server, getting files, such as CSV files or graphic files, created by
the R scripts from the server to the user’s machine requires special methods. Here we go through how to do
this.

1) Write this script into 000-common.R:

# define a folder for output files

user_file_path <- './user_output/'

# create a folder for files to be exported

if (!dir.exists( user_file_path )) dir.create( user_file_path, showWarnings = FALSE )

cat( normalizePath(user_file_path) )

Optionally, you can also use a function to add all "user’s files" into a zip file (arena_R_export.zip)
which can be downloaded (after running the project files). Add also this script into 000-common.R
(after the script above):

zip_user_files <- function(tFolder) {

#delete zip if it exists (i.e., file to be downloaded)

fn <- paste0( tFolder, "arena_R_export.zip ")

if (file.exists(fn)) {

#Delete file if it exists

file.remove(fn)

}

# check if any files to be zipped

f <- list.files(tFolder, all.files=TRUE, recursive=TRUE, full.names=FALSE)

if (length(f) > 0) {

zip::zip("arena_R_export.zip", f, recurse=TRUE , root=tFolder, include_directories = TRUE,
mode = "mirror")

}

}

Note: add script
zip_user_files( user_file_path )
into the very last calculation step.

2) in the part where you need to write something into a CSV file, use this type of command line

write.csv(my_DF, paste0( user_file_path, "test.csv" ), row.names = FALSE)

3) To download the files from the server, there are two methods:
a) using RStudio’s EXPORT tool (this is easier),
b) or by R coding.

a) RStudio’s EXPORT tool:

In the Files pane, More menu, there is an Export… option:

b) Coding method to export the files from the server:

file_list = list.files(path=user_file_path, pattern="*.csv")

for (i in seq_along(file_list)) {

export_filename = file_list[[i]]

# create a path for file to export

my_export_file_path <- paste0(user_file_path, export_filename)

# make a pause before exporting the next file, otherwise there can be a pop-up warning

if (i > 1) {

cat('*** PRESS ENTER HERE')

readLines(stdin(), 1)

}

# export to local disk using browser's capabilities

browseURL(my_export_file_path)

}

sections.title: Plot Grid Generator in making spatial Sampling Point Data
sections.text:
The Sampling Point Data is a lookup table that can be used to retrieve data into forms and tables. It can
contain for example the predefined list of sampling points, such as clusters and sample plots numbers. It can
also contain properties of these points, such as location (coordinates) and data derived from GIS or other
ancillary sources.

One handy method to generate a spatial grid for Arena is to use the Plot Grid Generator tool, that is available
via https://openforis.org/materials/ and Handy Shiny apps section.

This tool contains an User’s Guide.

Once the grid has been successfully generated, it can be exported as CSV files. The application writes a zip
file, that contains the following files:

The file "plot_points_Arena.csv" can look as follows:

This is a hierarchical category table that can be imported into Arena’s categories. Because "label" and
"description" do not contain any language codes, these fields will be written into the survey’s default
language, i.e. to the first language in the survey (properties).

* location_x, location_y, location_srs :  point coordinates in EPSG:4326 (latitude-
longitude)
* location_map_x, location_map_y, location_map_srs: point coordinates in imported map’s Spatial

sections.title: Installing Open Foris Arena on a Custom Server (1/2)
sections.text:
This section explains how to install and run Open Foris Arena on your own server (on-premises or cloud VM)
using Docker, instead of using the hosted openforis-arena.org platform. It is intended for system
administrators who will maintain the server.

1. Overview

Arena is distributed as a set of Docker images: the Arena application itself, a PostgreSQL/PostGIS database,
and, optionally, an RStudio Server container used for running custom R scripts on collected data. Running
Arena on a custom server therefore requires Docker and, unless you already have one, a PostgreSQL
database.
2. Prerequisites

●  A server (Linux is recommended) with a public or reachable IP address, if the server must be accessed
outside the local network.
●  Docker installed. Download and install it from docker.com if it is not already present.
●  Sufficient disk space for the database, uploaded files, and analysis output directories.
●  Network access from the server to the internet, to pull Docker images (or a local copy of the images
if the server is offline).
●  Optional: an SMTP or SendGrid/Office365/Amazon SES account, if Arena should send emails (e.g.,
password resets, survey invitations).

3. Install and configure PostgreSQL

If you do not already have a PostgreSQL database available, run one as a Docker container. The following
command creates a database named "arena" and a user "arena" with password "arena", listening on port
5444:
docker run -d --name arena-db -p 5444:5432 \
-e POSTGRES_DB=arena \
-e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=arena \
-e POSTGRES_USER=arena \
postgis/postgis:17-3.5

Note: Change the database name, user, password, and port to suit your environment and security
requirements. Arena can also be pointed at an already-existing PostgreSQL/PostGIS instance instead of a
dedicated container.

4. Create the configuration file (arena.env)

Create a text file named arena.env containing the parameters Arena needs at startup. The most commonly
used variables are listed below; the full list is available in the Arena GitHub repository.

Variable  Purpose  Example
ARENA_PORT  Port the web application listens 9090
on

PGHOST / PGPORT /  PostgreSQL connection  localhost / 5444 / arena / arena / arena
PGDATABASE / PGUSER /  parameters (or use
PGPASSWORD  DATABASE_URL)

TEMP_FOLDER  Folder for temporary uploaded /home/your_user/openforis/arena/upload
files

FILE_STORAGE_PATH  File-system folder for stored  /home/your_user/openforis/arena/files
files (omit to use DB or S3)

ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR  Folder shared with RStudio  /home/your_user/openforis/arena/analysis
Server for analysis output

USE_HTTPS  Set to true if requests are  false
forwarded to HTTPS by a
reverse proxy

ADMIN_EMAIL /  Credentials for the first system admin@example.org / temporary-password
ADMIN_PASSWORD  administrator account

A minimal working arena.env looks like this:
ARENA_PORT=9090

PGHOST=localhost
PGPORT=5444
PGDATABASE=arena
PGUSER=arena
PGPASSWORD=arena

TEMP_FOLDER=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/upload
FILE_STORAGE_PATH=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/files
ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR=/home/your_user/openforis/arena/analysis

USER_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET=replace-with-a-long-random-string
USE_HTTPS=false

ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.org
ADMIN_PASSWORD=replace-with-a-temporary-password

Security: ADMIN_PASSWORD is used only to create the first system administrator account. Change this
password from within Arena immediately after the first login, and consider removing it from the file
afterward.

5. Install and run Arena

From the folder containing arena.env, run:
docker run --env-file ./arena.env --network="host" openforis/arena:latest

This pulls the official Arena image and starts the container, exposing the web application on the port defined
by ARENA_PORT (9090 by default). Use the same command to restart Arena after it has been stopped.
6. Open Arena in the browser

Once the container is running, open:
http://localhost:9090

sections.title: Installing Open Foris Arena on a Custom Server (2/2)
sections.text:
(replace localhost with the server's hostname or IP address if connecting remotely). The Arena login form
should appear. On first startup, Arena automatically creates a system administrator account using
ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD from arena.env. Log in with those credentials and change the
password using the Change Password function inside Arena.
7. Optional: run RStudio Server for statistical analysis

To enable custom R scripts and calculation chains, run RStudio Server as a separate container, sharing the
ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR folder defined in arena.env:
docker run -d --name arena-rstudio --network=host \
-v ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR:/home/rstudio \
-e DISABLE_AUTH=true \
rocker/rstudio

Replace ANALYSIS_OUTPUT_DIR with the actual path used in arena.env. RStudio Server will be available at:
http://localhost:8787

To restart RStudio Server after a reboot or stop:
docker container restart arena-rstudio

Alternatively, an already-existing external RStudio Server (or RStudio Server Pro pool) can be connected by
setting RSTUDIO_SERVER_URL (and related RSTUDIO_* variables) in arena.env instead of running a local
container.
8. Recommended next steps

●  Configure HTTPS via a reverse proxy (e.g., Nginx or Traefik) in front of Arena, and set
USE_HTTPS=true in arena.env.
●  Set up an email service (SendGrid, Office365, or Amazon SES) so Arena can send account and
survey-invitation emails.
●  Schedule regular backups of the PostgreSQL database and the file-storage / analysis directories.
●  Review the ALLOW_USER_ACCESS_REQUEST, FILE_UPLOAD_LIMIT, and
JOB_QUEUE_CONCURRENCY settings to match your organization's needs.
